sections.label: Long-term national plans
sections.summary: Several plans, including defence transformation, net zero, aviation, maritime, transport, infrastructure and innovation, will take decades to complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A good number of these plans, especially the ones dealing with the transformation of our defence capabilities, implementing our net zero ambition, developing our sustainable aviation and maritime hubs, transport systems and infrastructural capabilities and building an innovation economy will take decades to complete.

sections.label: Singapore high trust country
sections.summary: Singapore is in a fortunate position as a high trust country, with relatively high trust in Government compared to many other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Indeed, today, Singapore is in a fortunate position to be a high trust country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I looked at the Edelman Trust Barometer 2023 that was reported on CNA on 15 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Trust in our Government as an institution was reported to be relatively high compared to a vast number of other countries.

sections.label: Trust during COVID-19 pandemic
sections.summary: Strong trust between people and Government during COVID-19 led to higher vaccination, low mortality and faster reopening than many other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, it is the strong trust between our people and our Government that led to higher levels of vaccination, which in turn ensured that we kept mortality rates low and allowed us to reopen our borders and rebuild our lives much faster than in many other countries.

sections.label: Baby Bonus cash gift appeal
sections.summary: An appeal was made for Mdm Zhu's baby Qi Yue, born seven hours before the enhanced Baby Bonus cash gift eligibility date of 14 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last month, I wrote an appeal on behalf of Mdm Zhu, who had just given birth to a baby girl, seeking the enhanced Baby Bonus cash gift as announced in Budget 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Her baby, Qi Yue, was born at 5.00 pm on 13 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This was seven hours too early as the enhanced Baby Bonus cash gift, which would have been disbursed seven to 10 days after registration of the baby’s birth, was meant for babies born on or after 14 February 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In fact, the Baby Bonus Cash Gift policy was designed to allow babies due to be born on or after 14 February 2023 but were delivered earlier to get enhanced cash gifts too.

sections.label: First quarter 2023 growth
sections.summary: MTI reported that the economy grew by only 0.1% in the first quarter of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) reported last Friday that our economy grew by only 0.1 % in the first quarter of 2023.

sections.label: Investments in children from humble backgrounds
sections.summary: The Government has made substantial investments in children from humble backgrounds, particularly at rental flats, through KiFAS and ComLink.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Government has already made substantial investments in our children from humble backgrounds, particularly at rental flats through programmes like the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) and the Community Link (ComLink).

sections.label: Bukit Batok study centre
sections.summary: Tava by Talent Beacon, a non-profit, sets up a study centre in Bukit Batok for children in rental flats, supported by MND and HDB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In Bukit Batok, we have one example in the form of Tava by Talent Beacon, which is a non-profit organisation that sets up a study centre specially for children living in our rental flats, with the support of MND and HDB.

sections.label: Tax-deductible donations stable
sections.summary: During MSF's COS debate, the speaker highlighted that tax-deductible donations per year stayed around $1 billion between FY2016 and FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: During the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)'s COS debate this year, I highlighted that over the past five years between FY2016 and FY2020, the amount of tax-deductible donations per year remained more or less stable at $1 billion.

sections.label: Access to expensive sports
sections.summary: Children from low- or middle-income backgrounds will find it difficult to access more expensive sports such as golf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The reality now is that children from low- or middle-income backgrounds will find it difficult to gain access to more expensive sports, such as golf.

sections.label: Foreign Interference Bill debate
sections.summary: The speaker says it may be useful to recount the House debate on the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, it may be useful to recount the debate that we had in this House on the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Bill.

sections.label: Perceived FICA party chasm
sections.summary: The public perceived a wider chasm between governing and opposition Members on FICA than was actually the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a result, the public perceived that there was a wide chasm between the hon Members of the governing and opposition parties on Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act (FICA) than what was, in fact, the case.

sections.label: Forward Singapore Exercise engagement
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore Exercise by the 4G leadership involves engaging thousands of Singaporeans from all walks of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As we all know, the Forward Singapore Exercise conducted by our 4G leadership involves engaging thousands of Singaporeans from all walks of life.

sections.label: 4G Team Forward Singapore engagement
sections.summary: The 4G Team should engage people so their views on the shared vision are taken onboard, with its Forward Singapore report expected in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It will serve the 4G Team well to engage such people so that their views on the shared vision for the future are taken onboard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I look forward to receiving the 4G Team’s report on the Forward Singapore Exercise that is expected to be issued in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Better services and social support
sections.summary: Education is deeper and social support tighter with more social spending per person than ever, and more is done in health, education, housing and transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Their education is deeper, their social support tighter and with more social spending per person than ever before in our history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In health, education, housing and transport, we are doing much more to provide all Singaporeans with better services and to support the more vulnerable groups.

sections.label: Prosperity and Singapore's survival
sections.summary: The two aims are to achieve prosperity for happiness and peace, and to ensure Singapore survives as an independent nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, to achieve prosperity so as to ensure happiness and peace for our people; and second, to ensure that Singapore continues to survive as an independent nation.

sections.label: No external guarantor of survival
sections.summary: There is nothing external, no partners or allies, that will ensure the survival of this improbable nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We are either annexed or merged and, in fact, we ourselves thought this at the start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: There is nothing external to ourselves, no partners or allies that will ensure the survival of this improbable nation.

sections.label: Taxing the rich and super cars
sections.summary: Taxing bequests heavily faces two constraints, but the rich can be taxed further, including a separate COE category for super cars over a million dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There are 2,700 billionaires in the world – their money comes, not only from their income from work but also through their ownership of capital – property, stocks and the businesses that they owned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We could reset the game after each round – tax bequests heavily so as to erode the advantages of inherited wealth – but there are two constraints on this: the first is to recognise the ancient instinct which urges us to strive so as to be able to leave something for our family as our legacy; the second is a practical benchmark – that Singapore must set tax regimes for the rich, with an eye on the rates in the rest of the world, rather than merely responding to local pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having said this, I do think that we can tax the rich further, especially in specific expenditures such as, super cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I asked this in my Budget debate speech and I ask the Finance Minister, at some point again, to consider a separate category of Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) for super cars costing over a million dollars.

sections.label: Gini coefficient fell in 2022
sections.summary: After adjusting for Government transfers and taxes, the Gini coefficient fell from 0.437 in 2021 to 0.378 in 2022, the second lowest on record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: After adjusting for Government transfers and taxes, the Gini coefficient fell from 0.437 in 2021 to 0.378 in 2022, the second lowest on record.

sections.label: Capital income and wealth data
sections.summary: A speaker notes capital income is likely more unevenly distributed and suggests the Government may release wealth distribution data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It does not take into account capital income which is likely to be more uneven in distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I do not know what the wealth distribution is in Singapore, but the Government may consider releasing some data so as to help public discussion.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit for lower-income group
sections.summary: A speaker says the SkillsFuture Credit framework should be further institutionalised with additional resources targeted at the 60% group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our SkillsFuture Credit framework that we have is good, but I think it should be further institutionalised with additional resources targeted for this 60% group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Five years ago, in 2018, also in response to the President's Address then, I had said that we must make sure that a boy born to poor parents must have more from the state than one born from the rich.

sections.label: Public pension spending compared
sections.summary: In 2017 Greece and Italy spent around 15.5% of GDP on public pensions, while the entire Singapore budget is about 18% today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2017, Greece and Italy spent around 15.5% of GDP on public pensions; Austria, France and Portugal spend around 13% to 14% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The entire Singapore budget is only about 18% today.

sections.label: Singapore's ranking in common currency
sections.summary: Measured in a common currency, Singapore comes in at fifth in 2022, ahead of Qatar and the US and just shy of Switzerland.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Measured in terms of a common currency, Singapore comes in at fifth in 2022, ahead of Qatar and the United States (US), and just shy of Switzerland.

sections.label: DBS studies on lower-income balances
sections.summary: Two DBS studies found close to half of lower-income groups suffered significant income falls, with around half dropping more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, two separate studies by DBS on account balances revealed that close to half of lower-income groups suffered significant falls in income, with around half within that group experiencing drops of more than 50% and had less than a month of emergency funds available.

sections.label: Inflation and wage increases
sections.summary: Inflation peaked at 7.5% in August and September, and a DBS survey found wage increases failed to keep up with inflation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Inflation hit hard, reaching peaks of 7.5% in August and September last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A more recent survey by DBS found that wage increases have failed to keep up with inflation and for the lowest income group, expenses have grown close to five-and-a-half times faster than their salaries.

sections.label: Official poverty line not established
sections.summary: The passage states that helping the poor requires knowing who they are, but Singapore has yet to establish an official poverty line.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Regardless of which school of thought one subscribes to, the fact remains that if we are to help the poor, we must know who they are.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But in Singapore, we have yet to establish an official poverty line.

sections.label: Differing income and expenditure thresholds
sections.summary: The passage lists HDB rental, ComCare and Department of Statistics thresholds, noting the basic needs figure is from two surveys ago and not updated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The HDB income threshold for rental happens to be $1,500, while the ComCare threshold is closer to $1,900.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Department of Statistics instead pegs the Average Household Expenditure on Basic Needs at $1,250, albeit this low figure was from two surveys ago and the calculation does not seem to have been updated.

sections.label: Call for official poverty line
sections.summary: The passage states life is about thriving and that all humans have aspirations, concluding it is time for an official poverty line.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Life is not just about making it day-to-day, but about thriving, as all humans, poor or not, have aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is time for an official poverty line.

sections.label: ComCare approval process criticised
sections.summary: The passage states that at this year's COS debate, the speaker suggested the ComCare approval process can be intrusive, onerous and demeaning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At this year's COS debate, I suggested that the ComCare approval process can be intrusive, onerous and demeaning.

sections.label: Short duration of support
sections.summary: The passage states that support is often granted for an unbearably short time of three to six months in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, support is often granted for an unbearably short time – three to six months in the first instance.

sections.label: Small payouts and low thresholds
sections.summary: The passage states topped-up amounts reach $350 a month at best, support hardly dents high costs, and low-income thresholds are $3,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even with the most recent revision, topped-up amounts come to $350 a month at best, and can be as little as half that.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While any additional help is undoubtedly welcome, I have had many residents share that the support hardly makes a dent in high cost Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is exacerbated by our low-income thresholds – $3,000 a year – before one is disqualified.

sections.label: Workfare and dependants
sections.summary: Workfare support is independent of dependants, unlike other jurisdictions where households with children receive significantly higher support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Were these individuals to work only limited hours, perhaps due to health or age, the limited additional support Workfare promises would nevertheless not be available to them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The WIS, to put it bluntly, is independent of dependants.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is in contrast to the approach in other jurisdictions where support is significantly higher if the household has one or more children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This approach makes absolute sense, since parents not only have more dependants to support, they also need to make arrangements for childcare were they to enter into the workforce formally.

sections.label: Silver Support age limit
sections.summary: Silver Support is available only to those aged 65 and above, and the speaker says more can be done.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: — how Silver Support is available only to those aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: We can do more, much more – if we want to truly call ourselves a first-world nation.

sections.label: Russia's breach of UN Charter
sections.summary: Russia's attack on Ukraine breached the UN Charter and the prohibition against the use of force, and the world should take a firm stand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Russia’s attack on Ukraine was a breach of the UN Charter and the prohibition against the use of force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The breach of the UN Charter by a charter member is worrying for the rule of law and it is important for the rest of the world to take a firm stand on this if we intend to maintain the rule of law.

sections.label: Rivalry threatening shared system
sections.summary: The rivalry between the two is now threatening the system on which both prospered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, the rivalry between the two is now threatening the system on which both prospered.

sections.label: Preschool attendance for lower-income children
sections.summary: Children who miss preschool, predominantly from lower-income families, start off on the back foot, so universal attendance should be encouraged or made compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This means those who miss preschool, who are predominantly from lower-income families, will start off on the back foot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is therefore even more important to ensure that preschool is attended by all children and either make this compulsory or have strong measures in place to encourage universal attendance.

sections.label: MSF assistance and tuition
sections.summary: MSF rarely gives financial assistance for such expenses, and other self-help groups provide support, but a system with less emphasis on tuition would be good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Of course, MSF rarely gives financial assistance to cope with such expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are other self-help groups that come in to provide support for this but it will be good if we can develop a system that places less emphasis on tuition.

sections.label: Parliament reopening and Tamil festival
sections.summary: The reopening of Parliament coincides with the Tamil Language Festival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: (In Tamil):   The reopening of Parliament this time coincides with the Tamil Language Festival.

sections.label: Shortage of Tamil teachers
sections.summary: A shortage of Tamil teachers in schools has arisen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One issue that has arisen now though is the shortage of Tamil teachers in schools.

sections.label: Combined Tamil classes
sections.summary: Some schools have been forced to combine Tamil classes with children from different subject-based bands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, because of the shortage of teachers, I understand some schools have been forced to combine Tamil classes with children in different subject-based bands coming together for the same class.

sections.label: Singapore education system changes
sections.summary: Singapore's education system has changed over the years, from streaming in 1981 to Full SBB from 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A lynchpin of our system of meritocracy is our education system, which is the subject of my speech today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore’s education system has gone through several changes over the years, from the introduction of streaming in 1981, to the introduction of Subject-based Banding (SBB) in 2014, to the roll out of Full SBB starting in 2020.

sections.label: Workers' Party through-train proposal
sections.summary: The Workers' Party proposed a 10-year through-train programme from Primary 1 to Secondary 4 to bypass the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast, the Workers’ Party has proposed a 10-year through-train programme from Primary 1 to Secondary 4 as an option for parents who want their child to bypass the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our proposed through-train programme gives students 10 years to prepare for their first major examination at Secondary 4, allowing them to learn at a pace suited for them while developing other areas of interest.

sections.label: Financial literacy survey findings
sections.summary: Surveys in 2021 and 2022 showed low financial literacy and lack of retirement planning among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a private sector survey in 2022, more than half of Singaporeans considered themselves “financially illiterate”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The same survey showed that financial literacy is the lowest among the age group of 18 to 24, at only 35%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the MoneySENSE National Financial Capability Survey 2021, four in 10 respondents said they lacked knowledge of basic financial concepts, such as risk diversification and simple and compound interest, and more than half had not developed a retirement plan.

sections.label: Household wealth in property
sections.summary: The Department of Statistics states almost half of Singapore's household wealth is in residential property assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics, almost half of Singapore’s household wealth is in residential property assets.

sections.label: Property returns and financial literacy
sections.summary: Other asset classes have generated returns comparable to residential real estate, so Singaporeans need better financial literacy for diversified portfolios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Contrary to the common perception, other asset classes have also generated returns comparable to Singapore's residential real estate, even in the Singapore property boom period, especially after factoring in costs related to holding and transacting properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As I had mentioned in my speech on the Motions on public housing in February, we need to moderate the growth in housing prices and ensure they do not outpace Singapore’s economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is unlikely that Singapore’s economic growth will be anywhere close to what was achieved in the past few decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is also unlikely that, moving forward, Singaporeans’ residential property assets can deliver a level of returns similar to what was previously achieved, without causing undue inflationary pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Equipping Singaporeans with better financial literacy will help them to become willing to have a more diversified asset portfolio and make more sound decisions while doing so, taking into consideration their risk profile and circumstances.

sections.label: Mind over hands professions
sections.summary: Professions of the mind have been over-prioritised over professions of the hands, leading to significant differences in remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, professions of the mind have been over-prioritised over professions of the hands and has led to significant differences in renumeration.

sections.label: Accelerating PWM worker wages
sections.summary: The Government, unions and industry are encouraged to consider accelerating wage increases of PWM workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to encourage the Government, unions and industry to consider accelerating the wage increases of our PWM workers.

sections.label: Proposed inheritance tax on property
sections.summary: A gradated inheritance tax on property above S$5 million is proposed, with exemptions for special needs beneficiaries and HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government can consider introducing a tax based on the percentage of the value of the property and the percentage of tax should be higher the more expensive the property inherited is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The minimum could begin from, say, a property value of S$5 million and gradated upwards from there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Inheritance tax in OECD countries can go as high as 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I would suggest more modest rates, perhaps in line with the additional buyers' stamp duties, that can go up to 25% for Singapore Citizens and 35% for foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The tax regime should be able to take into consideration the personal circumstances of beneficiaries and provide appropriate exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should, for example, be exemptions for beneficiaries with special needs and HDB flats should also be exempted from inheritance taxes – and hopefully, they will not reach that limit of S$5 million anyway!

sections.label: Administering inherited property tax
sections.summary: Taxes on inherited real property are easy to administer and may lower property prices by easing house price inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taxes on inherited real property are relatively easy to administer as valuation is straightforward and, in Singapore, transfer processes are transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Introducing such a tax may have a collateral benefit of lowering property prices by easing house price inflation and properties being put up for sale that may not have otherwise come up on the market.

sections.label: Career Progression Model for skilled trades
sections.summary: NTUC mooted the Career Progression Model in February 2023 to uplift skilled essential trades, prioritising plumbers, electricians and air-conditioner technicians.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In early February 2023, the NTUC Secretary-General mooted the Career Progression Model (CPM) as part of our efforts to uplift workers in skilled essential trades, to develop their skills, help them attain mastery and build long-term potential careers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: COVID-19 border restrictions revealed an urgent need to step up our efforts to uplift this sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: There are currently more than 50,000 local workers in skilled trades, ranging from electrical and electronic tradesmen, building and related trades workers, among others.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Labour Force Survey 2022, more than half of the craftsmen and related trades workers are currently above 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To start off, NTUC will prioritise three essential trades that have a direct impact on our daily lives – plumbers, electricians and air-conditioner technicians.

sections.label: Income support for job losses
sections.summary: NTUC will continue to advocate income support for those who lose their jobs, tied to active job seeking and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: They are also in a particularly precarious position should they lose their jobs, as they generally have more dependents and more financial responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We will continue to advocate income support for those who lose their jobs, tied to certain active job seeking and reskilling.

sections.label: Training allowances for mid-career workers
sections.summary: During the Budget debate, the speaker called for training allowances for mid-career workers undergoing the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: During the Budget debate, I have called for training allowances to be given to mid-career workers to give them greater peace of mind in undergoing longer and also undergoing the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sections.label: Company Training Committees win-win
sections.summary: CTCs are a win-win initiative for employers and workers, supported by the Government through the CTC grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: CTCs are a win-win initiative for employers and workers, supported firmly by the Government through the CTC grant.

sections.label: Support for platform workers
sections.summary: NTUC will work with tripartite partners through the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers to enhance retirement adequacy, housing security and work injury insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In addition, with the number of platform workers rising and the development of the gig economy, NTUC will work together with our tripartite partners, through the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers, to enhance the retirement adequacy, housing security and work injury insurance for our platform workers.

sections.label: Training allowances and Company Training Committees
sections.summary: The speaker asked for more training allowances and time, and NTUC has encouraged enterprises to set up Company Training Committees since 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: During the Budget debate, I have asked for more training allowances and training time so that workers can receive long-term and deeper training with peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In addition, since 2019, NTUC has encouraged enterprises to set up their Company Training Committee (CTC) to help the company to transform and upgrade and allow their employees to participate in training to upskill and transform.

sections.label: Labour Movement worker advocacy
sections.summary: The Labour Movement will keep advocating workers' interests by improving wages, welfare and work prospects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As the Labour Movement, we will continue to advocate workers’ interests through improving wages, welfare and work prospects.

sections.label: Labour Movement commitment to workers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement commits to putting workers first, giving them better job opportunities, assurances, protection and resilience to adapt, upskill and retrain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In the Labour Movement, our commitment is to always put workers first, ensure that workers will have better job opportunities, assurances and protection and the resilience to adapt, upskill and retrain themselves to remain relevant for the future.

sections.label: Legislation passed this Parliament term
sections.summary: This House debated and passed amendments to the Online Safety Act, the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act and formed the Digital and Intelligence Service of the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: During the first half of this Parliament term, this House has debated and passed various pieces of legislation to further put us in better stead to withstand against such potential external forces through amendments to the Online Safety Act, enactment of the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act and the formation of the Digital and Intelligence Service of the SAF.

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act
sections.summary: The Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act will consolidate legal powers from the Penal Code and Sedition Act to maintain racial harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, I am looking forward to the full implementation of the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act, first announced by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong during the 2021 National Day Rally speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new law is meant to consolidate all current legal powers dispersed across the Penal Code and Sedition Act to ensure the maintenance of racial harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will not only provide the powers to restrain someone from committing an offence regarding racism but also compel them to learn more about the other race.

sections.label: Changes to education system
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes education changes promoting social mixing, competency-based subject learning and value-based interactions in children's education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, I welcome the changes to our education system to promote greater social mixing and competency-based subject learning and the infusion of value-based interactions and engagements in our children's educational journey.

sections.label: Uplifting measures and social mobility
sections.summary: Uplifting measures help those needing a hand to upgrade and upskill, with more help through housing, healthcare and social welfare policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am glad that we have provided various uplifting measures that allow those who need a helping hand to get the boost they need to upgrade and upskill themselves in the path towards social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The last term of our Parliament session has also seen the Government afford more help through housing, healthcare and social welfare policies, passing legislation to form the Public Defender's Office to allow greater access to criminal justice and changes to the Misuse of Drugs Act, which affords greater vigilance against the scourge of drug abuse, especially on the vulnerable segments of our society.

sections.label: Unity on core national interests
sections.summary: The speaker urges rejecting divisive language and agrees with the President's call for unity regardless of race, religion or political affiliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We cannot allow these to seep into the language of our politics and divide us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I concur with the President's call for all of us to close ranks and stand united regardless of race, religion or political affiliation, especially when it comes to core national interests.

sections.label: Budget support for inflation
sections.summary: Comprehensive Budget support measures were implemented to cover the inflation-induced increase in spending for lower- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They see interest rates, prices and bills going up and impacting their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why I had implemented comprehensive support measures in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These measures will help to cover the inflation-induced increase in spending for lower- and middle-income households.

sections.label: Key shifts in social compact
sections.summary: The speaker lists key shifts for a new social compact: skills, success, social support, seniors, and renewed commitment to one another.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, I will share some of the key shifts that we will embark on as part of our new social compact: a new approach on skills; a new definition of success; a new approach for social support; a new approach to caring for our seniors; and a renewed commitment to one another – less about "I" and "me", more about "us" and "we".

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART nationwide
sections.summary: The KidSTART programme is being scaled up nationwide to reach more lower-income parents and close early gaps in children's lives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We know that the first few years matter greatly in shaping a child's potential.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we are scaling up the KidSTART programme nationwide to reach out to more lower-income parents and to close the early gaps in our children's lives.

sections.label: End of PSLE T-scores, streams
sections.summary: PSLE T-scores are a thing of the past, and so will be the Normal (Technical), Normal (Academic) and Express stream labels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, PSLE T-scores are a thing of the past.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So will be the labels of Normal (Technical), Normal (Academic) and Express streams.

sections.label: Major changes to SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Some headway has been made, but more remains to be done, so major changes to strengthen SkillsFuture are being looked at.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have made some headway since then, but there is still much more to be done.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are therefore looking at major changes to strengthen SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Professionalising skilled trades
sections.summary: It states that one specific way is to further professionalise skilled trades such as electricians and plumbers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One specific way is to further professionalise skilled trades, like electricians and plumbers.

sections.label: Uplifting lower-wage workers
sections.summary: It states that many lower-wage workers serve in essential services and that Workfare and the PWM will continue to raise wages, set a skills ladder and provide upgrading opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many of them serve in essential services, like security, lift maintenance and cleaning.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have been doing much to uplift lower-wage workers through Workfare and the PWM, and we will continue to do so: increase wages, set out a skills ladder, and provide opportunities to upgrade.

sections.label: Fresh Start Housing Scheme support
sections.summary: It states that Mr Gan and Mdm Chai received personalised support and financial guidance, a $35,000 Fresh Start Housing Grant, and CPF-serviced loan repayments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mr Gan and Mdm Chai joined the Fresh Start Housing Scheme and received personalised support and financial guidance from HDB and social service officers (SSOs) throughout their home ownership journey.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They received a $35,000 Fresh Start Housing Grant and the rest of the loan will be fully serviced by their CPF contributions.

sections.label: Reducing SPED financial burden
sections.summary: It states that the aim is to reduce the financial burden on parents of children attending special education schools and care centres.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, we want to reduce the financial burden on parents of children attending special education (SPED) schools and care centres.

sections.label: Ramping up BTO supply
sections.summary: It states that efforts are being spared to ramp up Build-To-Order flat supply and catch up on COVID-19 delays.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We know that housing is top-of-mind – we have discussed this recently in Parliament, in the housing debate, and in the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are sparing no effort to ramp up the supply of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and to catch up on the delays caused by COVID-19.

sections.label: Targeted re-employment scheme design
sections.summary: It states that a targeted re-employment scheme is wanted to provide assurance, reduce strain on displaced workers, and still encourage upskilling and job search.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We know that automatic unemployment benefits can, and have, often led to negative outcomes elsewhere, because displaced workers who receive generous benefits may find it more attractive to stay unemployed, rather than to get back into the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we want to design a support scheme that provides assurance but avoids these negative outcomes: a targeted re-employment scheme that will reduce the strain on displaced workers to make ends meet, while still encouraging them to continue with their upskilling and job search.

sections.label: Ageing Singapore population
sections.summary: By the end of this decade, one in four Singaporeans will be above 65.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By the end of this decade, one in four Singaporeans will be above 65, as Members are well aware.

sections.label: Ageing infrastructure investments
sections.summary: The Government will invest in infrastructure such as Community Care Apartments, Active Ageing Centres, home-based care and community partnerships against loneliness.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will not be possible for everyone, but I believe we can make it possible for most.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we will invest in our infrastructure to make this happen: build more Community Care Apartments; expand the network of Active Ageing Centres; improve access to home-based care services; and work with community partners to prevent loneliness and social isolation.

sections.label: Government role in CPF
sections.summary: The Government now plays a larger role in CPF through higher interest for lower balances, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government, in fact, now plays a larger role in CPF through higher interest for those with lower CPF balances, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, as well as supplementing CPF payouts with Silver Support.

sections.label: Work, mental health, families
sections.summary: Moves include flexible work arrangements, kindness and compassion for mental health, and a conducive environment for families, with paternity leave increased this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Be it working out flexible work arrangements; treating ourselves and one another with greater kindness and compassion, knowing that good mental health is a key part of good health overall, or creating a conducive environment for Singaporeans to start and nurture families.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We made some moves in the Budget this year, such as increasing paternity leave and we will consider what more can be done.

sections.label: No comprehensive universal welfare
sections.summary: Other governments spend above 40% of GDP versus 18% in Singapore, but Singapore does not intend to adopt comprehensive universal welfare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Their governments typically spend above 40% of their Gross Domestic Product (GDP), compared to 18% in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Some may think this is a good model for Singapore, but from our point of view, from the Government's point of view, it is very clear: we do not intend to adopt such a model of comprehensive universal welfare.

sections.label: Middle-income real incomes
sections.summary: Singapore's middle-income group now has higher real incomes than the US, most European societies, Japan, Hong Kong and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The middle-income group in Singapore now has higher real incomes – real incomes after netting off inflations – than in many other places; higher than the US and most European societies and well above that in other advanced Asian societies, like Japan, Hong Kong and South Korea.

sections.label: GST and Budget funding gap
sections.summary: The PAP Government says it will state how it raises revenues to keep the Budget balanced, and without GST there will be a huge funding gap.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When we plan to spend more, the PAP Government will always tell you plainly how we propose to raise revenues and ensure that our Budget remains balanced over the medium-term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We do not need to go through the detailed arguments again.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But without the GST, which the WP still does not support – and I am not even talking about the increase in GST, but the entire GST which the WP still does not support – we will face a huge funding gap.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: None of the alternatives that the WP has suggested will make up for the shortfall.

sections.label: Refreshed social compact as compass
sections.summary: The refreshed social compact will be the compass for the road ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our refreshed social compact will be our compass for the road ahead.

sections.label: Message to Singaporeans on challenges
sections.summary: The message to Singaporeans is that no challenge or obstacle cannot be overcome, and Singapore can move forward together as one people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Faced with the stark realities of a troubled world, my message to Singaporeans is simple: there is no challenge we cannot overcome; no obstacle we cannot deal with.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We can move forward together as one people.

sections.label: FWAs and women workers
sections.summary: FWAs can enhance workplace productivity and let companies retain women workers and attract women returners, of whom 240,000 are not in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: FWAs can enhance workplace productivity and can allow companies to retain women workers in the workplace and attract women returners back; of which by the way, there are 240,000 women of economic age not in the workforce today.

sections.label: Support for shifting caregiving norms
sections.summary: More practical support must be given to shift cultural caregiving norms, and the Labour Movement appreciates that shared parental leave and increased paternity leave were accepted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More practical support must be given to help move the needle in shifting cultural caregiving norms and the Labour Movement is appreciative that our workers' suggestions of shared parental leave and increasing paternity leave have been accepted by our tripartite partners.

sections.label: Tripartite support for FWA requests
sections.summary: The Labour Movement thanks the Tripartite Partnership for supporting and legislating in the near future workers' rights for individual FWA requests to be considered by employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement thanks the Tripartite Partnership in supporting and legislating in the near future, our workers' rights for individual FWA requests to be considered by employers.

sections.label: Platform workers protection and representation
sections.summary: The Tripartite Partnership formed a platform workers Advisory Committee to look into protection and representation of gig platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To a platform owner, the impact of a rise in platform fees of less than 50 cents, could be minimal in consolidated amounts, but to the driver or to the rider, the accompanying decrease in ride or delivery orders, will mean decreased earnings and less food on the table for their families, sometimes even for weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement has been championing the cause of our freelance and self-employed for many years now and in the face of a fast-evolving gig landscape, the Tripartite Partnership has formed the platform workers Advisory Committee to look into the protection and representation of our gig platform workers.

sections.label: Setting up Special Needs Trust
sections.summary: The speaker and volunteers spent five days setting up paperwork, visiting banks and getting lawyers for a Special Needs Trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Together with my volunteers, we spent the next five days setting up the necessary paperwork for him, visiting banks, getting the lawyers in, setting up a Special Needs Trust.

sections.label: Trust set up before death
sections.summary: Through community contacts things were put in order, and he passed on that night after signing the trust agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Thankfully, things went smoothly and through community contacts, we managed to get things in order for him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: He passed on that night after he signed the trust agreement, which actually took the longest to set up.

sections.label: More support for special needs adults
sections.summary: The speaker says more must be done for special needs adults and their caregivers after coordinating safety nets for Mr Y's son.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Through understanding his wishes for his son and the hoops we had to jump through to coordinate the safety nets needed to protect Mr Y's son, I know that we need to do more for our special needs adults and their caregivers.

sections.label: Mother Tongue proficiency census figure
sections.summary: According to the 2020 Census of Population, 74.3% of Singaporeans are proficient in their respective Mother Tongue languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to the 2020 Census of Population, 74.3% of Singaporeans are proficient in their respective Mother Tongue languages.

sections.label: Referral to job assistance agencies
sections.summary: Referred workers are channelled to agencies like e2i, LearningHub and SMCCI for job placement and skills upgrading courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Through a referral process, these workers are channelled to multiple agencies for assistance, such as NTUC's e2i and LearningHub, as well as the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI).

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By doing so, jobseekers are given access to job placement opportunities and skills upgrading courses, which can help improve their chances of securing better employment opportunities.

sections.label: NTUC M3 worker upskilling
sections.summary: FA4 illustrates NTUC and M3's commitment to ensuring workers upskill and adapt to changing work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: FA4 is just one example that illustrates how NTUC and M3 are committed to ensuring that workers are upskilling and adapting to the changing nature of work.

sections.label: EveryWorkerMatters Conversations launch
sections.summary: Gaps remain, especially for vulnerable groups, so #EveryWorkerMatters Conversations was launched to engage workers on the future of work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We acknowledge that there are still gaps that need to be addressed, especially in supporting vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is why we launched the #EveryWorkerMatters Conversations, which aims to engage workers from all walks of life to collectively define the workers' compact and hear their views on the future of work.

sections.label: Company Training Committees effort
sections.summary: CTCs involve unions and employers identifying skills gaps and scaling up reskilling, training and career progression, with more CTCs wanted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As underscored by Deputy Secretary-General Mr Desmond Tan, one such effort by the Labour Movement is the Company Training Committees (CTCs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: These CTCs involve unions and employers working closely together to identify skills gaps and look into scaling up on reskilling, training and career progression for their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this vein, we want to form more CTCs to help businesses build a skilled and adaptable workforce.

sections.label: Randstad survey job loss worry
sections.summary: The latest Randstad survey reported that 48% of Singapore respondents worry about losing their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The latest Randstad survey reported that 48% of respondents in Singapore are worried about losing their jobs.

sections.label: Job skills replaced by AI
sections.summary: Researchers found 37% of average job skills were replaced in five years, and ChatGPT marks generative AI reaching many companies and consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Researchers have found that 37% of the average job skills have been replaced just over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: ChatGPT marks the first significant milestone that generative artificial intelligence (AI) is placed in the hands of many companies and consumers.

sections.label: Single poverty line problems
sections.summary: Helping needy Singaporeans must continue, but a single poverty line has inherent problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I agree that we must continue to work our hardest to help our needy Singaporeans and work must not stop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But the suggestion of having a single poverty line has inherent problems.

sections.label: Median gross monthly income increase
sections.summary: Median gross monthly income increased by more than $400 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With the tightness, actually, our median gross monthly income has increased in 2022 by more than $400.

sections.label: Absentee payroll funding increase
sections.summary: One way is to increase absentee payroll funding and the overall $100,000 annual cap for companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One of the ways is to increase absentee payroll funding and the overall $100,000 annual cap for companies.

sections.label: SSG course support and cap
sections.summary: Support for SSG-funded certifiable courses is fixed at $4.50 per hour, with an organisation cap of S$100,000 per calendar year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, there is a fixed level of support for SSG-funded certifiable courses at $4.50 per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The organisation's cap is also limited to S$100,000 per calendar year.

sections.label: Strengthening social safety net
sections.summary: The country and workforce will be affected, so the social safety net must be actively strengthened for Singaporeans at every stage of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our country and workforce will also be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We must actively strengthen the social safety net to give Singaporeans the confidence to move forward at every stage of their lives.

sections.label: Support for the unemployed
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will help the unemployed receive training, such as Career Conversation Programmes, and calls for increased subsidies during unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For the unemployed, I hope that the Government will help them receive training during unemployment, such as the Career Conversation Programmes (CCPs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I also call on the Government to increase subsidies for the unemployed during this period.

sections.label: Growth, jobs and safety nets
sections.summary: Good growth, good jobs and strong social safety nets are key to helping Singaporeans navigate a rapidly changing economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Good growth, good jobs and strong social safety nets are key to helping Singaporeans navigate the vagaries and vicissitudes of a rapidly changing economy.

sections.label: MSF sets assistance duration limits
sections.summary: The three- to six-month limit on short- and medium-term assistance is decided by MSF, not by others.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: For example, the three- to six-month limit on short- and medium-term assistance is not decided by them but by MSF.

sections.label: ComCare support, thresholds and criteria
sections.summary: Residents received support beyond three to six months, and MSF announced $640 monthly for one-person Long Term Assistance households, with Short Term criteria unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: In the cases that I have seen, I have seen residents who have gotten support beyond three to six months, some even longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: We have also provided our residents through schemes with CDC through our WeCare support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: So, I think it is not true that the MSF scheme necessarily handicaps or that we constrain our officers in the help they can dispense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: I also want to extend once again that if the Member has families in Sengkang that require assistance, I will be more than happy to assist them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And just to quote exactly what I said in my speech, which was, I suggested and I quote, "to peg all thresholds for Government assistance, especially ComCare to this line or higher but never lower." So, the idea is that you would have a clear benchmark to map it to and you could have multiples to allow for these various tailored solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last August, MSF announced that a one-person household on the ComCare Long Term Assistance scheme will receive a cash assistance of $640 per month or an increase of 6.25% from the previous cash amount of $600 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The qualifying criteria for Short Term Financial Assistance remain at a household income of not more than $1,900 per month or a per capita income of not more than $650 per month.

sections.label: MSF financial assistance spending figures
sections.summary: MSF will spend $601 million on long- and short-term financial assistance, including ComCare administration manpower costs, about 0.6% of the 2023 Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: MSF will be spending $601 million on long- and short-term financial assistance, including the manpower costs to administer the ComCare Assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: This represents about 0.6% of Singapore's 2023 Budget or only 0.1% of Singapore's GDP.

sections.label: ComCare short-term criteria revision example
sections.summary: The qualifying criteria for ComCare short-term assistance can be revised by 10%, letting applicants with per capita monthly household income of not more than $715 qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the qualifying criteria for ComCare short-term assistance can be revised by 10% so that applicants with per capita monthly household income of not more than $715 can qualify.

sections.label: OECD Learning Compass transformative competencies
sections.summary: The OECD Learning Compass 2030 identified three transformative competencies: creating new value, reconciling tensions and dilemmas, and taking responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The OECD Learning Compass 2030 has identified three “transformative competencies” that students and learners need in order to contribute to and thrive in our world and to shape a better future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These are: creating new value; reconciling tensions and dilemmas; and taking responsibility.

sections.label: More formative, less summative assessment
sections.summary: The speaker suggests increasing focus on formative assessments such as coursework and less on summative assessments like examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For our students to develop this competency, I would suggest that we increase the focus on formative assessments, such as coursework, and less on summative assessments like examinations.

sections.label: PSLE coursework and exam scores
sections.summary: Urges MOE to make each Primary 6 student's final score a combination of coursework and PSLE examination score.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But what I would like to surface again for consideration is to urge the Ministry of Education (MOE) that has done great work so far in being progressive towards the PSLE and looking at different ways of scoring and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But I would like to urge MOE to see how they can make each Primary 6 student a final combination of coursework and their PSLE examination score.

sections.label: Ethnic diversity in public service leadership
sections.summary: Hopes for more ethnic diversity among senior public service leaders to be more representative of Singapore's ethnic mix.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am not suggesting, Mr Speaker, that we should resort to tokenism or to just have someone in a position because he or she is of a particular ethnicity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, if the Government is one of our largest employers and if the senior public leaders are responsible for formulating key policies that would be responsible for taking Singapore forward into the next few decades and beyond, then I would hope there could be more ethnic diversity among the Permanent Secretaries, Deputy Permanent Secretaries, Statutory Board Chief Executives and Deputy Chief Executives, as well as other senior leaders in the Uniformed Services in a manner that would be more representative of the ethnic mix of Singapore society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Greater diversity in Public Service leadership would not just result in diverse perspectives, less groupthink and a richer quality of strategic decisions; it also introduces role models that Public Service officers of every background can relate to and look up to.

sections.label: Equality, equity and redistribution
sections.summary: States those who need more should be given more, and describes equality as foundation and equity as levelling the playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, those in our community who need more should be given more, especially from those who can afford more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is something that the Government has been moving progressively towards in their more nuanced and differentiated taxation and redistribution policies over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If equality sets the foundation of creating an equal playing field, then equity levels out the playing field by identifying disparities to ensure that everyone has what they need to achieve success.

sections.label: Inclusive models for differentiated learning needs
sections.summary: Hopes for more integrative inclusive models where students with differentiated learning needs study together with more neurotypical students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While it is good, for example, to have dedicated schools to cater to those with special and unique learning needs, I hope that we can continue to work towards more integrative inclusive models where we can have students with differentiated learning needs studying together with those with more neurotypical backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Learning to care for your fellow student starts that journey towards developing empathy, kindness, compassion and generosity which, in turn, teaches you to care for your colleague, your neighbour and even a stranger in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This, I believe, will see us not only moving forward together, but doing so in a manner that reflects our commitment to being a kinder, caring and compassionate Singapore where – to echo Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong – it is less about "I", "me" and "my" and more about "we", "us" and "ours".

sections.label: AI generating photo-realistic images
sections.summary: Notes that a year ago software generating photo-realistic images from text seemed far off, but now ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Midjourney 5 exist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Just one year ago, if you said software could generate photo-realistic images of scenes and events which never happened just through some text instructions written and keyed in via a keyboard, you might have been told that was some way off.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And yet, today, we have ChatGPT, GPT-4 architecture, Midjourney 5 – and that is just one year on.

sections.label: AI challenges for social trust
sections.summary: States that AI will pose great challenges for social togetherness and social trust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: AI will pose great challenges for social togetherness and social trust.

sections.label: Foreign troublemakers using deepfakes
sections.summary: Foreign troublemakers may try to damage society by circulating deepfakes of community incidents and opinion shapers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: You can imagine how foreign troublemakers will try to damage our society – circulating deepfakes of community incidents that never happened, deepfakes of opinion shapers or people in the news.

sections.label: Social cohesion under AI disruption
sections.summary: Policymakers not thinking about strengthening social cohesion will see business-as-usual policies weaken social togetherness in an AI-disrupted world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If you are a policymaker and you are not already thinking about how to strengthen social cohesion in this brave new world, then business-as-usual policies will actually mean the progressive weakening of our social togetherness in a world disrupted by AI and generative AI.

sections.label: Neighbourhood centres and hawker centres
sections.summary: It asks whether policymakers favour more hawker centres and coffee shops to bring people together, or let the market decide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: When neighbourhood centres are designed and outfitted, do policymakers lean in favour of having more hawker centres and coffee shops as a way of bringing people together, even building, designing ahead of demand, or does the market get to decide after the fact?

sections.label: AI customising student learning
sections.summary: AI can customise learning to each student's skills, but this does not mean teachers will become obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: With AI, it will be possible to customise the learning process to each student's individual skills, understanding what works best for that particular student.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This does not mean teachers will become obsolete.

sections.label: Human relationships amid AI disruption
sections.summary: It calls for public policy to bring Singaporeans together for face-to-face interactions, strengthening human relationships and trust amid AI disruption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It means educators could have more time to befriend students, understand each student's journey, be that cheerleader, that mentor, that shoulder to cry on in times of difficulty, or that person to motivate the student to grow beyond what they dreamed they could do.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to make sure our Public Service deeply understands AI and its opportunities, whether in health, whether in defence, but across the board in policymaking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Amid a world of AIs, deep fakes and generative AI creations, we need to double down in our public policy on how we bring people together, on how we bring fellow Singaporeans together for these face-to-face interactions, which will be the key bedrock foundation of our society and inoculation against deep fakes and other AI disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to strengthen human relationships, deepen human trust and we need policy to guide that direction in a world of AI disruption, so that amid big changes in the world, Singapore and Singaporeans continue having that sense of togetherness so that we can survive and thrive in a dangerous world and continue to dream and overcome whatever the world throws at us.

sections.label: MOE addendum on preschool education
sections.summary: MOE's addendum commits to quality education and more investment in preschool education, especially for children from disadvantaged families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education's (MOE's) addendum to the President's Address outlines its commitment to quality education and strong foundation for every child, while breaking new ground to adapt to the changing landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is heartening that MOE will invest more in preschool education especially for children from disadvantaged families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that access to quality childcare and early childhood education develops foundational skills and helps boost math and reading in children.

sections.label: Subject-Based Banding in secondary schools
sections.summary: Subject-Based Banding lets secondary school students learn subjects based on their strengths and learning needs, catering to diverse interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: An example is Subject-Based Banding (SBB), which caters to the diverse interest and needs of students by allowing secondary school students to learn subjects based on their strengths and learning needs.

sections.label: Rethinking work structure for workers
sections.summary: Tapping workforce diversity requires rethinking work structure so learning and training are systemic for workers of different ages and life stages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is an advantage if we are able to tap the diversity of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I have made this point in several of my speeches in this House, that we need to rethink the structure of work to make learning and training systemic for workers of different age groups and stages of life.

sections.label: Flexible work and retirement age shifts
sections.summary: Attracting and retaining workers requires fundamental shifts in mindsets and policies on work arrangements, including flexible work arrangements and retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These can provide opportunities to attract and retain workers as well as tap a larger pool of talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But to do so, will require fundamental shifts in mindsets and policies around work arrangements, including flexible work arrangements (FWAs) and even retirement age.

sections.label: Means-testing caregiving support criteria
sections.summary: Means-testing qualifying criteria for caregiving support for middle-income Singaporeans may work against some middle-income families caring for family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Means-testing qualifying criteria for caregiving support for middle-income Singaporeans may work against some middle-income families that care for their family members.

sections.label: Review eldercare support qualifying criteria
sections.summary: Mdm Lee's mother and brother would qualify for eldercare support if living in an HDB flat, so a review of qualifying criteria is appealed for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The irony is that if Mdm Lee's brother or mother did not live with Mdm Lee but instead lived in a Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat, her mother and brother would qualify for support for eldercare services and nursing home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But Mdm Lee and her family believe that staying together contributes to the overall well-being and care of their mother and brother.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I appeal for a review of the criteria to qualify for support for eldercare services, intermediate and long-term, to better support families as they care for their loved ones.

sections.label: WHO Global Report on Ageism
sections.summary: The WHO's Global Report on Ageism 2021 states about one in two persons worldwide harbours ageist attitudes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the World Health Organization's (WHO's) Global Report on Ageism 2021, about one out of every two persons worldwide habours ageist attitudes.

sections.label: MOM survey on ageist attitudes
