sections.summary: A survey released last March by the Ministry of Manpower confirmed ageist attitudes were still prevalent in the Singapore workplace, affecting older workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, in a survey released last March, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) confirmed that ageist attitudes were still prevalent in the Singapore workplace, affecting older workers.

sections.label: Awaiting anti-discrimination legislation
sections.summary: The speaker says they are still awaiting the anti-discrimination legislation announced by the Prime Minister nearly two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, for stronger protection for all workers, we are still eagerly awaiting the anti-discrimination legislation, which the Prime Minister announced nearly two years ago.

sections.label: Inter-generational contacts and mixed HDB blocks
sections.summary: The speaker supports HDB's move to mixed blocks of flats for seniors and younger families, and cites a WHO-noted initiative pairing seniors with young people for video games.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for increasing inter-generational contacts, I fully support the HDB's move to evolve from building blocks with only senior apartments, to having mixed blocks of flats for seniors and flats owned by younger families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another Singapore initiative was cited positively by the WHO – that of pairing seniors from activity centres with young people to play video games together.

sections.label: Lowering voting age to 18
sections.summary: The speaker believes the voting age should be lowered from 21 to 18, noting Singapore is among a handful of countries that has not done so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I believe one change that should be made is to give younger cohorts a direct say in our national elections by lowering the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I raised this matter in this House 16 years ago and most recently again in this year's Committee of Supply debates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is despite Singapore being among a handful of countries in the world that has not reduced its voting age to 18 years, such as Bahrain, Cameroon, Tonga and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

sections.label: National Service and voting age
sections.summary: It could be argued that requiring male Singaporeans to serve National Service at 18 but vote only at 21 is a form of age-based discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, it could well be argued that when we require male Singaporeans to serve National Service at 18 years, but only permit them to vote at 21 years, this is a form of age-based discrimination.

sections.label: Primary and secondary school affiliations
sections.summary: Increasing affiliations between a primary and secondary school can lift the burden of thinking about which school to go on to after the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Increasing affiliations between a primary and secondary school can lift the burden of thinking about which school to go on to after the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

sections.label: Customising teaching, smaller class sizes
sections.summary: MOE's addendum focuses on customising teaching for students of differing abilities, and the speaker believes smaller class sizes would let teachers spend more time with each student.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MOE's addendum to the President's Address, focuses on being able to better customise teaching and learning for students of differing abilities, to bring out the best in each child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe one way this can be accomplished, is to have a smaller class size to allow teachers to have more time with each student.

sections.label: Reducing class sizes needs more teachers
sections.summary: The speaker says reducing class sizes would require more teachers and calls it a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of course, reducing class sizes must mean we need more teachers and I believe it will be a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Transnational nature of scams
sections.summary: The challenge is accentuated by the transnational nature of scams, with 90% from overseas and scammers technologically savvy in using digital platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What accentuates this challenge is the transnational nature of the issue: with 90% of the scams from overseas and how technologically savvy the scammers are in using various digital platforms to carry out the scams.

sections.label: Suggested anti-scam solutions
sections.summary: The speaker suggests solutions including transaction limits, phone calls to account owners, spotting suspicious patterns in consecutive transactions, and a bank-activated kill switch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of just saying what the problem is, I humbly suggest some solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These include placing limits on transactions, giving phone calls to owners of bank accounts to ensure that they do want to proceed on a transaction, spotting suspicious patterns in consecutive transactions and a kill switch which can be activated by the bank if it detects multiple and suspicious outflows of monies from citizens' accounts.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Command recovery figures
sections.summary: The Anti-Scam Command froze 16,700 bank accounts last year and recovered over $146 million, out of 31,728 scams in 2022 and over $660 million reported stolen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Anti-Scam Command has taken the commendable lead in this in freezing 16,700 bank accounts just last year and recovering over $146 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But that is out of 31,728 scams just in 2022 and over $660 million were reported to have been stolen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For many of the elderly who are scammed, the loss is often at least six figures, which is close to their entire retirement savings.

sections.label: Weak accountability, survey on influence
sections.summary: Vertical and horizontal accountability remains weak, and a 2010 book cites survey data showing 56% of Singaporeans agree they lack power to influence Government policy or actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Vertical and horizontal accountability remains weak." Published research from the book "The Well-being of Singaporeans" by Tambyah, Tan and Kay, in 2010, reaches similar conclusions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They cite survey data to show that 56% of Singaporeans agree with the statement that, generally speaking, people like me do not have the power to influence Government policy or actions, while another 23% are neutral.

sections.label: Opposition alternatives to GST and housing
sections.summary: The Opposition explained alternatives to a GST hike and to a housing ecosystem based on asset appreciation, which would weaken the resale market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During very major recent debates in this House, the Opposition explained how there were alternatives to a Goods and Services Tax (GST) hike that would slow the rate of growth of the Reserves; and that there were alternatives to a housing ecosystem based on the promise of asset appreciation and that these alternatives would lead to some weakening in the resale market.

sections.label: Transparency for rational political discourse
sections.summary: Rational political discourse requires transparency, but Parliamentary Questions often do not elicit requested information and public consultation outcomes are sometimes not public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, to have rational political discourse, we need transparency of information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are many examples of Parliamentary Questions that do not elicit the information requested without an explanation as to why that is the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sometimes, outcomes of public consultation are not made public.

sections.label: Edelman Trust Barometer Singapore economic optimism
sections.summary: The 2023 Edelman survey found only 36% in Singapore felt their families would be better off economically in five years, the lowest since surveying began.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the 2023 Edelman Trust Barometer survey, only 36% of respondents in Singapore felt that their families will be better off economically in five years' time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only 36%, the lowest level for this measure since Edelman started surveying 23 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This 36%, for Singapore, compares with the 40% global average across 24 countries.

sections.label: Poverty and inequality survey concern
sections.summary: A 2020 Ipsos national survey ranked poverty and social inequality as the third big area of concern, after jobs and healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, poverty and social inequality ranked as the third big area of concern in a national survey done in 2020 by Ipsos, after jobs and healthcare.

sections.label: Call for CPI data by demographic group
sections.summary: The speaker previously called in the House for Consumer Price Index data to be published by demographic group, as inflation affects groups differently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Previously in the House, I have called for Consumer Price Index (CPI) data to be published by demographic group, for example, parents with young children or empty nesters, as inflation affects these groups differently.

sections.label: Reforming HDB housing and BTO prices
sections.summary: The speaker proposes reforming the HDB housing system to lower Build-To-Order prices by revisiting the land valuation formula and other reforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Four, reforming the HDB housing system to lower Build-To-Order (BTO) prices by revisiting the formula for land valuation as well as introducing various other reforms, as we argued in the recent housing debate.

sections.label: Reserves growth trade-offs
sections.summary: These ideas together will slow the rate of growth of the Reserves but will not draw down the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lest anyone say that the trade-offs have not been explained, these ideas, taken together, will slow the rate of growth of the Reserves, but will not draw down the Reserves.

sections.label: Opposition healthcare and housing claims
sections.summary: The speaker says they championed an expansive acute hospital bill insurance scheme and permanently delinking BTO from resale prices before the PAP Government adopted these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, I only have less than five minutes left.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We championed an expansive acute hospital bill insurance scheme and permanently delinking BTO from resale prices long before this was adopted by the PAP Government.

sections.label: UAE renewables dealplomacy
sections.summary: UAE sovereign wealth fund renewables arm targets 100 gigawatts by 2030, and Masdar committed to a 10-gigawatt Egypt wind farm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The scale of this is extremely large – just the renewables arm of one of their sovereign wealth funds have targeted 100 gigawatts of renewables at home and abroad by 2030, quadrupling the current commitment and being worth around US$100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An example of UAE "dealplomacy" is where its government-owned renewables business, Masdar, committed to a 10-gigwatt mega-wind farm in Egypt in a deal on COP27's sidelines, which would save Egypt $5 billion in annual gas costs and offset about 9% of its emissions.

sections.label: Southeast Asia renewables savings
sections.summary: IRENA estimates Southeast Asia renewables could save US$160 billion and $1.5 trillion in health and environmental costs by 2050, needing $7 trillion investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The International Renewable Energy Agency estimates that, if Southeast Asia were to build enough renewables to cut energy-related carbon dioxide emissions, it could also save US$160 billion as well as $1.5 trillion in health and environmental costs related to fossil fuels by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But to pull this off, $7 trillion in investment is needed from now, till then.

sections.label: Clarification on voting age remarks
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that the Minister did not say people between 18 and 21 lacked the skillsets to vote.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I just wish to make a point of clarification to Ms Sylvia Lim's speech.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I heard the Member saying that the Government essentially said that people under 21 years old did not have the skills to vote.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Because if I am right – I just checked the Hansard – on 24 February 2023, in my reply to Ms Sylvia Lim's question, I said, "If we look at the rights and responsibility of all our people from the ages of 16 until 21, there is a gradation of scale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In fact, I had raised my hand with Deputy Speaker because I also went back to check and I realised that my recollection of the response was not quite accurate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I accept what the Minister has said – the Minister did not say that the people between 18 and 21 did not have the skillsets to vote, but what the Minister said was that there is a different rights and responsibilities for people between 16 and 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But I believe the question still remains as to whether those between 18 and 21 should be empowered to vote.

sections.label: Age discrimination legislation
sections.summary: The interim report and update was recently issued, and age discrimination and ageism will be addressed in legislation next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The interim report and update was recently issued and I look forward to seeing this piece of legislation next year, when it is introduced in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The issue of age discrimination and ageism as highlighted by hon Member Sylvia Lim is one area which will be addressed in this piece of legislation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training revenue productivity benefits
sections.summary: SSG and MTI study found companies using SkillsFuture for training report revenue benefits and higher productivity, and Labour Movement research found business leaders saw positive worker changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Results from a study conducted by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) showed that companies which tap on SkillsFuture to fund eligible training expenses report revenue benefits and higher productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Our research in the Labour Movement also revealed that majority of business leaders have observed positive changes in their workers post-training, such as higher performance at work and being able to take on new job responsibilities.

sections.label: Career coach accreditation and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: The speaker proposes industry-led accreditation of career coaches and counsellors and expanding SkillsFuture Credit to include engaging professional career coaches and counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, such individualised career services are either availed to the high-potential segments of a company, only in large organisations and multinational corporations (MNCs) or those who are retrenched or unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the same vein, there is a lack of industry-led accreditation of career coaches and coaching in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As we navigate a skills and employment landscape that is increasingly complex, the assistance and guidance by a career coach is becoming more of a necessity than a luxury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose that there be industry-led accreditation of career coaches and counsellors and expanding SkillsFuture Credit utilisation to include the engaging of professional career coaches and counsellors.

sections.label: Extending support beyond pandemic
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes mention that the Government would study extending support beyond the pandemic, similar to the COVID-19 Recovery Grant and SGUnited Jobs and Skills programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this respect, I welcome Mdm President's mention and Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's speech yesterday, which alluded that the Government would study how we will extend support beyond the pandemic – well, similar to the COVID‐19 Recovery Grant and the SGUnited Jobs and Skills programme, to watch our backs and help our workers tide over unemployment and get re-employed again.

sections.label: 10-year through-train programme bypassing PSLE
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Phua agree that a 10-year through-train programme from Primary 1 to Secondary 4 would help parents whose children bypass the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have not had the chance to check the Hansard yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But be that as it may and in the interest of arriving at the best policies for Singaporeans, regardless of who raised it first, do Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Phua agree that the 10-year through-train programme from Primary 1 to Secondary 4 would be a helpful option for parents who want their children to bypass the PSLE?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I mentioned about MOE's response to this idea and suggestion by the hon Member Denise Phua.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: There are constraints because the Member is looking at the whole continuum from primary to secondary school.

sections.label: Pilot integrated 10-year programme
sections.summary: The speaker still sees potential in a pilot integrated 10-year programme to do away with the PSLE, but acknowledges challenges and suggests continuing in Forward Singapore conversations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In response to hon Member Gerald Giam's question, I still think that there is potential good pathway to do away with the PSLE and have a pilot of an integrated 10-year programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But I also acknowledge the challenges that Education Minister Chan Chun Seng mentioned in this year's Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, the debate should not be on just having or not having that pathway, but really to go on to the next level, perhaps in the Forward Singapore conversations.

sections.label: Singapore ranked best business environment
sections.summary: The Economic Intelligence Unit ranked Singapore for the 15th consecutive year as the world's best business environment over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Economic Intelligence Unit recently just ranked Singapore for the 15th consecutive year, as the world's best business environment over the next five years.

sections.label: Foreign workforce and social compact
sections.summary: Singapore needs a large foreign complementary workforce, with foreign residents forming 38% of the labour force and 27% of residents, amid the Forward Singapore exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To keep our economy vibrant and to support the needs of our ageing population, Singapore needs a large pool of foreign complementary workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the foreign residents today constitute 38% of the labour force and represent 27% of all residents in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is, indeed, at a point of inflexion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is timely that the whole-of-Government has engaged Singaporeans in the Forward Singapore exercise, led by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and the 4G leaders, as a start to the refresh of our social compact.

sections.label: Hiring based on paper qualifications
sections.summary: Most Singapore employers recruit, pay, promote and advance employees based primarily on paper qualification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Most of our employers in Singapore recruit, pay, promote and advance their employees based only on paper qualification primarily.

sections.label: KidSTART and after-school study halls
sections.summary: The Government's commitment to KidSTART and similar programmes is right, and MOE is asked to invest in after-school study halls for older students needing help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the Government's commitment to KidSTART and other programmes, which help to uplift the children in the lower-income households and give them an equal chance early in life to participate on a level playing field, is the absolute right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And for older students who may need extra help but cannot afford tuition, I would like to propose that MOE invest in some kind of after-school "study halls", facilitated by teachers and student ambassadors to help these students with their revision, homework and preparation for examinations.

sections.label: Government scholarships and bond penalties
sections.summary: The Government could rethink scholarship purposes, give more to students with merit and financial need, and the Public Service Commission could review bond-breaking penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government might want to rethink the purpose of Government scholarships and perhaps, consider giving more scholarships to students who both have merit and financial need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Public Service Commission may also want to review the penalties for persons breaking bond and make them punitive enough, likened to defaulting their National Service commitments, so as to incentivise the right behaviours and values.

sections.label: Scholars serving bond in SMEs
sections.summary: The Government is recommended to send its scholars to serve their bond in local small- and medium-sized enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another recommendation I have, is for the Government to send their scholars to serve their bond in local small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

sections.label: Class sizes and tax rebates
sections.summary: With falling enrolments, MOE is asked to consider reducing class sizes to under 30, and the Government to consider tax rebates for singles sponsoring nieces' or nephews' education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we have falling enrolments due to fewer babies born each year, one proposal that I hope MOE can consider and I heard it in the House just now as well, is to bring down class sizes to less than 30 students per class.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider giving tax rebates to singles – the aunts and the uncles – who sponsor their nieces or nephews for their continuous education or tuition, in the same way like deductions for foreign domestic helpers in the tax form?

sections.label: Internships and apprenticeships for students
sections.summary: Almost all polytechnic and ITE students can do internships, and more can be done to incentivise companies to hire them as apprentices before graduation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, almost all students have the opportunities to do internships and attachments with companies as part of their polytechnic or ITE education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think that more can be done to incentivise companies to hire our polytechnic and ITE students as apprentices even before graduation and; for the companies' on-the-job training to be certified as stackable modules toward the diploma course which the students are pursuing, or even toward professional qualifications later on.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills pivot
sections.summary: More companies are needed, and SGUnited Jobs and Skills can pivot to incentivise companies to employ polytechnic and ITE students as apprentices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we need more companies to come on board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is where I see SGUnited Jobs and Skills, which was effectively applied during COVID-19, can pivot to incentivise companies to employ our polytechnic and ITE students as apprentices and progress them to full-time jobs after graduation.

sections.label: Parliamentary questions and motions
sections.summary: The party asked over 300 Parliamentary Questions, tabled two Motions on jobs and public housing, and three Adjournment Motions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among many other actions, we have asked more than 300 Parliamentary Questions; tabled two full Motions on jobs and public housing; and three Adjournment Motions, questioning vaccination-differentiated measures, public expenditures on the Sports Hub and SPH Media Trust and the Selective En Bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS) at Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3.

sections.label: Employment Pass and diversity proposals
sections.summary: Proposed policies include an EP levy of $1,200 monthly, higher EP and SP qualifying salaries, and diversity quotas limiting workforce percentage from any nationality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some of the specific policies that we have proposed in the last session of this Parliament include, an Employment Pass (EP) levy of $1,200 per month, increasing the qualifying salaries for EP and Special Pass (SP) holders in stages over three years to $10,000 and $4,500 respectively; and to implement diversity quotas that limit the total percentage of a company's workforce from any given nationality.

sections.label: MOM policy initiatives and exemptions
sections.summary: MOM introduced workplace fairness legislation, COMPASS and higher EP qualifying salaries, but many exemptions undermine these policies due to MOM's enforcement discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the last session of Parliament, the MOM has introduced many policy initiatives under the leadership of Minister Tan See Leng, such as the new workplace fairness legislation, the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) and an increase in minimum EP qualifying salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the many exemptions granted undermine the effectiveness of these policies, as the MOM is given a large discretion on how to enforce these policies.

sections.label: PSP housing policy proposals
sections.summary: Despite limited resources, the PSP put up two key policy proposals to reset housing policy: the Affordable Home Scheme and Millennial Apartment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Despite our very limited resources, the PSP has put up two key policy proposals to reset our housing policy – the Affordable Home Scheme and the Millennial Apartment Scheme.

sections.label: VERS and lease-decay details
sections.summary: The speaker questions why the Government has not announced further details for VERS or other lease-decay solutions in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For a government which prides itself on efficiency and not shying away from politically difficult decisions, it is hard to understand why the Government has not announced further details for the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS) or other solutions for the lease-decay problem in the past five years.

sections.label: Lowering voting age to 18
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party says it has supported lowering the voting age to 18 since its founding and repeats the call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To recognise this, the Progress Singapore Party has supported lowering the voting age to 18, since our party was founded; and I repeat this call today.

sections.label: PSP alternative policies on housing
sections.summary: PSP supports an open economy with controlled labour and capital movement, and will propose alternative policies on jobs and affordable public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While we support an open economy, with the free movement of labour and capital, such movements must be carefully controlled and calibrated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the housing market, we must ensure that public housing remains affordable and accessible and that rising land prices, due to an influx of wealthy foreigners who are allowed to purchase private property, do not cascade down into the HDB resale market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP believes that we need to have a new set of alternative policies that will serve us better going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the last Session of this Parliament, we have proposed some of those alternative policies for providing good jobs and affordable public housing to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As members of a responsible Opposition party, Ms Hazel Poa and I will continue to propose more alternative policies for the rest of our term as NCMPs.

sections.label: Preschool education and KidSTART
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MSF's addendum on preschool education and cites KidSTART's support for children from low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Government has made significant strides in improving early childhood education.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF's) addendum outlining plans to strengthen preschool education and ensure affordable and accessible quality childcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The KidSTART programme, for example, has successfully provided early childhood development support for children from low-income families, helping to level the playing field and give these children a better chance at success.

sections.label: Mental health services affordability
sections.summary: The speaker commends mental health efforts and suggests enhancing affordability and availability of services through subsidies and heartland expansion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The efforts by the Inter-agency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being and expanding mental health services in polyclinics are commendable examples.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As we forge ahead, I would like to suggest a few areas for consideration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We can achieve this by enhancing the affordability and availability of mental health services through Government subsidies and expanding such services in the heartlands.

sections.label: Healthier SG preventive care
sections.summary: Through Healthier SG, the Government will enhance preventive care and empower citizens to manage their health and undergo regular screening.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Through Healthier SG, the Government will enhance preventive care and empower citizens to manage their own health and undergo regular screening.

sections.label: Speaker's weight loss journey
sections.summary: The speaker was told through health screenings that he was overweight based on BMI and lost 15 kilogrammes, maintaining the weight since.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Last year, although I did not "appear" fat but through health screenings, I was told that, based on the Body Mass Index (BMI), I was overweight and I needed to make a major change in lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am grateful that I managed to lose 15 kilogrammes and have managed to maintain the same weight since then.

sections.label: Pilot training programme for coaches
sections.summary: A six-week pilot training programme for coaches will be launched to build a network promoting healthy living activities, with HPB support under Focus Area 5.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the end of the month, a pilot training programme for coaches lasting six weeks will be launched to build a network of like-minded community leaders to promote and manage healthy living activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We aim to equip them with basic knowledge about healthier lifestyle programs and ways to plan programmes that are suitable for the demographics of their respective towns.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They will also be trained to manage the Healthy Investment programme with the support of the Health Promotion Board (HPB), as part of the new Focus Area 5 area within M3.

sections.label: Uplifting lower-income families
sections.summary: The Government will strengthen policies to uplift lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government will strengthen our policies to uplift lower-income families.

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART
sections.summary: Over 6,000 children have benefited from KidSTART since 2016, and it will be scaled up nationwide by 2026 with priority preschool enrolment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since we started KidSTART in 2016, over 6,000 children have benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will intensify our efforts to start children from lower-income families on the right path.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will scale up KidSTART nationwide by 2026 and continue to facilitate priority enrolment for children from lower-income families in Anchor Operator Preschools and MOE Kindergartens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Investing in the early years is not just good science, it is also fiscally prudent.

sections.label: Expanding and integrating ComLink
sections.summary: ComLink expanded from four pilot towns in 2019 to 21 communities, integrating programmes and introducing scheme bundles for lower-income families on ComCare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From four pilot towns in 2019, we have expanded ComLink islandwide to 21 ComLink communities, each supported by a Social Service Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are further integrating social programmes under ComLink, such as KidSTART, UPLIFT Community Network and Project Dian@M3, so that families receive support from a single touchpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To make it easier for families to receive the support they need, we introduced scheme bundles so that lower-income families on ComCare assistance can access other assistances easily.

sections.label: Tax deduction for donations
sections.summary: The tax deduction rate of 250% for donations has been extended until end-2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We recognise that philanthropists, foundations and other entities, like family offices, also want to do good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We have extended our tax deduction rate of 250% for donations until end-2026.

sections.label: KidSTART practitioner training programme
sections.summary: SUSS worked with ECDA to launch a training programme equipping KidSTART practitioners to support children from lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For example, drawing on its know-how in early childhood education and social work, the Singapore University of Social Sciences worked with the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) to launch a training programme to equip KidSTART practitioners with the knowledge and skills to better support the development of children from lower-income families.

sections.label: Coordinating efforts under ComLink
sections.summary: Efforts to support families have been organised and coordinated collectively under ComLink over the past few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Over the past few years, we have expended significant efforts to organise ourselves better to support families, coordinating our collective efforts under ComLink.

sections.label: Companies and students supporting families
sections.summary: Companies provide mentorship and internships, while NUS students serve as ComLink befrienders in ComLink@Jurong West.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Companies step in to provide mentorship and internship opportunities to the youth to nurture and grow their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I have seen a glimpse of what is possible in ComLink@Jurong West, where UOL-Pan Pacific Hotels Group provides opportunities for children from lower-income families to access their facilities and enrichment classes through the National University of Singapore's (NUS') students stepping forward as ComLink befrienders to journey with families.

sections.label: MENDAKI volunteers and tuition programmes
sections.summary: MENDAKI mobilised volunteers for programmes like the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme and KelasMateMatika, and 99% of Malay students complete at least 10 years of education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: MENDAKI successfully mobilised the energies and passion of its many volunteers to drive programmes, like the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme and KelasMateMatika, for students across all levels today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, 99% of every Malay student cohort completes at least 10 years of education.

sections.label: Early childhood development and Project Dian
sections.summary: Singapore's strategy includes preschool enrolment by around age three, Project Dian@M3, priority enrolment, and Dian Ambassadors visiting families fortnightly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Therefore, a key aspect of our strategy to sustain social mobility in Singapore is early childhood development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We must ensure that children are enrolled in preschool by around age three.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are doubling down on our efforts to support families with young children through Project Dian@M3 and will also facilitate priority enrolment for children from lower income families into Anchor Operator preschools and MOE Kindergartens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our Dian Ambassadors have started visiting these families fortnightly, working with families to read with their children and support the parents in being involved in the development of their young children.

sections.label: Definition of social compact
sections.summary: A social compact is responsibilities towards one another, how work is rewarded, fruits distributed, and how people relate to and respect one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A social compact, is simply our responsibilities towards one another, how we reward work and distribute the fruits of labour and success, and how we relate to and respect one another.

sections.label: Meritocracy and evolving metrics
sections.summary: Singapore's relevance depends on evolving, so meritocracy based on a single static metric cannot build a resilient society with diverse strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Indeed, our relevance and competitiveness as a country depend on our ability to evolve with the times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Hence, meritocracy based on any single, static and narrow metric for talent and ability, will not allow us to build a resilient society with a diversity of strengths to meet tomorrow's challenges.

sections.label: Continuous meritocracy system
sections.summary: Society must have continuous meritocracy where no single test or point in time determines the rest of one's life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For society to allow everyone to do justice to their gifts, we must have a system of continuous meritocracy where no single test or point in time determines the rest of one's life.

sections.label: Wealth and privilege transfer
sections.summary: Access to opportunities and rewards could increasingly be determined by transfer of wealth and privileges from previous generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Access to opportunities and rewards could increasingly be determined not just by the merits of this generation, but the transfer of wealth and privileges from the previous generations.

sections.label: Six strategies for meritocracy
sections.summary: Government and people will focus on six strategies, moving away from single metrics, with Full SBB making education more flexible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To keep our Singaporean meritocracy resilient and sustainable, this Government, together with our people, will focus on six key strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will continue to move away from evaluating our people's diverse abilities by any single, static and narrow metric – be it the PSLE results, grade-point averages or whether they hold a degree or diploma.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: With the implementation of Full SBB next year, our education system will become more flexible and provide multiple pathways to cater to different learner profiles.

sections.label: University degree participation rate
sections.summary: Publicly-funded university degrees will have a higher lifetime cohort participation rate so more Singaporeans can obtain degrees during working lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our publicly-funded university degrees will also have a higher lifetime cohort participation rate so that more Singaporeans can look forward to obtaining a degree from our autonomous universities – not necessarily before starting work but at some point in their working lives.

sections.label: CET and SkillsFuture investment
sections.summary: The Government has increased its investment in CET in recent years, including through the national SkillsFuture movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To support this, the Government has increased its investment in recent years in CET, including through the national SkillsFuture movement.

sections.label: Training support for mid-career workers
sections.summary: Ideas include targeted training support for mid-career workers, such as SkillsFuture Credit top-ups and more accessible training for working adults.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Amongst the various ideas are more targeted training support for mid-career workers, including SkillsFuture Credit top-ups and how we make training more accessible for working adults with competing commitments and responsibilities.

sections.label: Special Education sector remuneration review
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing remuneration and career progression pathways in the Special Education sector to strengthen special needs educators' development and service quality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As an example, MOE is reviewing the remuneration and career progression pathways in the Special Education sector to strengthen the professional development of our special needs educators and improve the quality of services to better support students with special education needs.

sections.label: UPLIFT and progressive tax system
sections.summary: The Government set up the UPLIFT taskforce to rally community partners in helping disadvantaged students, supported by a progressive tax system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This has been and this will continue to be the guiding principle behind this Government's policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: That is why we set up the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT), to rally the community to partner our schools in helping students from disadvantaged backgrounds to progress educationally and to achieve their full potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: That is also why we have a progressive tax system to contribute to the running of such initiatives.

sections.label: Measure of societal success
sections.summary: The ultimate measure of success is how few people need help because they have been enabled to thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The ultimate measure of our success as a society is not how many people we can help because they are unable to keep up, but how few people we need to help because we have enabled them to thrive.

sections.label: Strengthening school cluster system
sections.summary: The school cluster system will be strengthened to pool and share resources, letting more students benefit from wider networks and social capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will further strengthen our school cluster system to enable better pooling and sharing of resources and allow more students to benefit from wider networks and build their social capital.

sections.label: Alumni sharing networks with schools
sections.summary: Alumni of more established schools are called on to share networks and opportunities with students in other schools and the wider community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Share your networks and opportunities with the next generation of students, not just in your alma mater but in other schools as well, to help them succeed like you did.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I, therefore, call on the alumni of the more established schools to come forward, to step forward – to join hands with us – to contribute to the wider community of schools so that we can all progress together, faster and better.

sections.label: Solidarity, responsibility and lifelong upskilling
sections.summary: The passage calls for strengthening solidarity and collective assurance while preserving individual responsibility and agency, and for helping everyone upskill and give back.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In an increasingly unequal and uncertain world, we need to strengthen our sense of solidarity and collective assurance without eroding the individual's responsibility and sense of agency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We must come together as individuals, as partners, as employers and as a community to celebrate diverse forms of abilities and contributions, to recognise and respect the dignity of those who contribute in different ways to society, to help everyone upskill continually and move up the ladder throughout our lifetimes and to give back to society and others who have helped us along the way.

sections.label: Success for next generation and meritocracy
sections.summary: The passage states success includes enabling the next generation to be more successful and building a resilient meritocratic society, and notes one in 150 children in Singapore has autism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The mark of our success is not just how well we enable this generation to achieve success, but how well we establish the conditions for the next generation to be even more successful than us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Only so will we be able to continuously write new chapters of the Singapore Story.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There may never be a perfect system to develop all the perfect students or workers for our societal needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But, we can all contribute our part to build a better or less imperfect system to continually inspire our people and all who believe in our dream to build a resilient and sustainable meritocratic system to bring out the best from all – to be a beacon of cohesion with unity of purpose in a troubled world; a society with a sense of collective responsibility towards one another; a society with respect for diverse abilities; a society that rewards hard work and talent; a society that recognises contributions beyond achievements; a society with gratitude for our blessings to want to do good for all beyond ourselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And finally, a nation confident to defy the odds of history to survive and thrive beyond SG100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One in 150 children in Singapore has autism, higher than the global average of one in 160 but lower compared to countries, such as the US, Japan, Denmark and Australia, which is one in 60 to 70.

sections.label: Trust services and insurance for autism
sections.summary: The passage states this includes sharing SNTC trust services supported by MSF and available insurance coverage, and urges Government to work with insurers to improve insurance access for persons with autism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This includes sharing with them the trust services of Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) supported by MSF and available insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to work with the insurers to improve access to insurance coverage for persons with autism.

sections.label: Autism daycare programme in community spaces
sections.summary: The passage states the Autism Association (Singapore)'s new daycare activity programme using community spaces such as public libraries and schools addresses lack of capacity in daycare activity centres for those over 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new daycare activity programme by the Autism Association (Singapore) making use of community spaces, such as public libraries and schools, to address the issue of the lack of capacity in daycare activity centres for those over 18 years old is a good start.

sections.label: Support for companies' R&D and global growth
sections.summary: The passage states the global business environment will become more difficult and notes the Government will provide more support to promising companies, including customised financial support for local companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The global business environment will become more difficult for us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am heartened that our Government will provide more support to promising companies, including customised financial support for local companies to build sustained research and development (R&D) and innovation capacity and to go global and grow into Singapore global enterprises.

sections.label: Decarbonisation, SME emissions and COE costs
sections.summary: The passage states decarbonisation provides business opportunities and calls for Enterprise Singapore to help SMEs measure emissions, while noting SMEs need to keep down business costs including vehicle COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Decarbonisation provides generation-defining business opportunities and our Singaporean companies are well-positioned to lead the way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need Enterprise Singapore to provide more assistance to SMEs so that they know how to measure emissions as many MNCs have started to request their SMEs suppliers to furnish their carbon emission data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SMEs need to keep down their business costs, of which their vehicles' COEs constitute a portion, a big portion.

sections.label: COE bidding by individual buyers
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to allow only individual buyers or companies needing COEs to bid, which may lower Category C COE prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If only individual buyers or companies, which need COEs, are allowed to bid for them, it may bring down the COE prices of Category C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can consider this suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They are unable to hire enough Singaporean workers to meet their operational needs and are struggling to stay in business, even if they have enough demand and clients.

sections.label: Reopening Parliament and renewing commitment
sections.summary: The passage states that reopening Parliament is a timely moment to refresh focus and renew commitment to the people and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As we reopen the Parliament, it is indeed timely to refresh our focus and renew our commitment to our people and Singapore.

sections.label: LinkedIn skills change in Singapore
sections.summary: LinkedIn's Future of Skills reports that skills needed in Singapore's technology, information and media industry changed by 36.8% between 2015 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For instance, according to LinkedIn's "Future of Skills", skills needed in the technology, information and media industry in Singapore have changed by 36.8% between 2015 and 2022 – just a span of seven years.

sections.label: Expanding SkillsFuture credits question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government would expand SkillsFuture credits to enable this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Would the Government expand the SkillsFuture credits to enable this?

sections.label: Goldman Sachs AI job replacement estimate
sections.summary: Goldman Sachs estimated that AI can replace 300 million full-time jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Goldman Sachs estimated that AI can replace 300 million full-time jobs.

sections.label: Governments duty to draw line
sections.summary: The passage states that governments around the world have a duty to draw that line, coordinate legislation and enforce it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this case, Governments around the world have a duty to draw that line, coordinate legislation and enforce it.

sections.label: Social contribution requirements for investors
sections.summary: The passage proposes requiring Global Investment Programme applicants and Tech Pass holders to commit to lecturing, mentoring start-ups and adopting community programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But we want them to do more than just putting money here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We should make it an explicit requirement for them to contribute socially and to integrate more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, requiring the Global Investment Programme applicants and Tech Pass holders to commit to: (a) delivering lectures to tertiary students or civil servants every year to enhance frontier industry knowledge; (b) mentoring local start-ups; and (c) adopting a community or charitable programme.

sections.label: Scholarships for senior learners
sections.summary: The passage suggests introducing scholarships for seniors to pursue tertiary diplomas or degrees and celebrating these mature graduands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In embracing lifelong learning, we could introduce scholarships for seniors to pursue tertiary diplomas or degrees and celebrate these mature graduands, so that the scholarships are not just limited to youths or young people, but to our mature Singaporeans as well.

sections.label: Diversity of voices in debates
sections.summary: The passage states debates must allow diversity of voices to illuminate facts and find common ground, not deepen social fissures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: During debates, we must allow diversity of voices so that issues can be considered comprehensively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But we must do so with the aim of illuminating the facts, explaining the trade-offs and bringing everyone to a common ground, not to drive wedges and deepen social fissures that will fracture our nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What we have today was painstakingly built over a whole lifetime and more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But to destroy this, could be as short as within just one day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In February, news broke that Anglo-Chinese School (Primary), or ACS Primary, would relocate to Tengah in 2030.

sections.label: Equal access to quality education
sections.summary: The passage states steps taken to ensure all children have equal access to quality education, including removing PSLE T-scores, Full SBB and expanded KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must do our best to ensure that all children have equal access to quality education in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have taken many bold steps in this – from removing PSLE T-scores to introducing Full SBB.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have also introduced an expanded KidSTART which seeks to provide a strong foundation for children from low-income households in Singapore by aiding their parents and caregivers in early childhood development.

sections.label: Raising wages of care workers
sections.summary: The passage states change must be reflected in remuneration and notes DPM Lawrence Wong and Minister Chan reiterated calls to increase wages of skilled and care workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To truly alleviate the dignity of such work or, in the alternative, to make such work viable for the highly capable among us to consider taking up, change must be reflected in the remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am heartened that Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Chan reiterated that call in their speeches to make sure that the wages of skilled and care workers will be increased to reflect the mastery of their skills.

sections.label: Humans, care skills and meritocracy
sections.summary: The passage states humans offer knowledge, technical and care skills surpassing robots, and a compassionate meritocracy requires policy changes and a mindset shift.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even in a highly automated world, humans are still able to offer a blend of knowledge, technical and care skills that surpass any present robot we have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As someone who works in the healthcare field, it is plain to see that robots just cannot replace the need for care and empathy from another human.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, achieving a broader, open and compassionate meritocracy in Singapore requires not only policy changes but also a fundamental mindset shift.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must recognise that every individual has something to offer and we must be willing to acknowledge and remunerate them for it.

sections.label: SkillsFuture series course attendance
sections.summary: Last year, 32,000 individuals attended SkillsFuture series courses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Last year, 32,000 individuals attended SkillsFuture series courses.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Ambassadors and career coaching
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Ambassadors advise Singaporeans on courses and programmes, and Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion to use SkillsFuture credits for career coaching will be studied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We also have a team of SkillsFuture Ambassadors on the ground to provide advice to Singaporeans, who want to learn more about the courses and programmes available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will study Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion to allow Singaporeans to use SkillsFuture credits for career coaching services.

sections.label: Labour market and job security
sections.summary: The labour market posted strong growth last year, with full employment, long-term unemployment at 0.7%, and resident employment higher than pre-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Moving to the subject of job security, our labour market move has posted strong growth last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We are at full employment, with long-term unemployment at 0.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Our resident employment is higher now than it was pre-pandemic.

sections.label: Paternity and infant care leave
sections.summary: From 2024, Government-paid paternity leave doubles to four weeks and unpaid infant care leave rises from six to 12 days per parent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: From 2024 onwards, Government-paid paternity leave will be doubled to four weeks and unpaid infant care leave will be increased from six days to 12 days per parent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Taken together, this means a working couple will have up to 26 weeks of leave in their child's first year.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on flexible work
sections.summary: MOM and tripartite partners will introduce Tripartite Guidelines by 2024 requiring employers to consider flexible work arrangement requests fairly and properly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To entrench flexible work arrangements, MOM and the tripartite partners will introduce a set of Tripartite Guidelines by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Guidelines will require employers to consider requests for FWAs fairly and properly.

sections.label: Community initiatives helping families
sections.summary: Community initiatives such as mental well-being circles, mentorships, free tuition, grocery distributions and caregiver respite help families in need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Community initiatives, such as mental well-being circles, mentorships, free tuition, grocery distributions and respite for caregivers, are just some of the many examples of how the community can chip in to help families in need.

sections.label: Refreshed social compact and family support
sections.summary: Wong spoke of a refreshed social compact of collective responsibility, and the Government enhanced Baby Bonus, Child Development Account First Step and Baby Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong spoke about the refreshed social compact of collective responsibility, where we need to be less about "me" and more about "we".

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to find ways to support families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will do our best to build a more caring and inclusive society with affordable housing, healthcare, childcare and education to cater to the different needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To help defray the cost of raising children, we have also enhanced the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, Child Development Account First Step and Baby Support Grant for eligible Singaporean children.

sections.label: Trust after COVID-19 pandemic
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Mdm President that Singapore is one of few countries where Government-people trust strengthened after the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Indeed, I agree with Mdm President that Singapore is one of the few countries in the world where trust between the Government and the people had strengthened after emerging from the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Closing last mile assistance gap
sections.summary: The Government has implemented sound policies, but some needing help fall through the cracks, so local community leaders and private sector helping hands are needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government has implemented sound policies and measures but, sometimes, those who need help fall through the cracks for all kinds of reasons and we need to identify local community leaders and helping hands, including those in the private sector, who can close the gap in the last mile of assistance delivery.

sections.label: Neighbours and volunteers bridging gap
sections.summary: Plugging the last mile gap can determine success or failure, and often a neighbour or volunteer less constrained by rules can close the loop.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The ability to plug the gap in the last mile can determine the success or failure of our measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Very often, the person to bridge the gap is a neighbour or a volunteer who is not as constrained by the rules and regulations of the system and can thus take certain steps to close the loop.

sections.label: Seniors in every Singapore household
sections.summary: Every household in Singapore will eventually have a senior member, and by 2030 one in four Singaporeans is projected to be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must address the reality that every household in Singapore will eventually have a senior member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is projected that by 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Flexible work options for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker fully supports more flexible work options for seniors, such as sabbatical leave, job-sharing, micro jobs and phased retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I fully support the call for more flexible work options for seniors, as previously emphasised in my Committee of Supply speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are several ways that we can implement these options, such as sabbatical leave, job-sharing, micro jobs and phased retirement.

sections.label: Government lead on workplace concepts
sections.summary: The Government should lead in implementing concepts with minimal disruption and introduce them into more workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government should take the lead and show how they can be implemented with minimal disruption while still reaping the benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to take more proactive measures to introduce and incorporate these concepts into more places of employment.

sections.label: Caregiver training courses and providers
sections.summary: Over 40 training providers offer more than 200 Caregivers Training Grant-approved courses so caregivers can look after loved ones competently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is to ensure that caregivers have the necessary skills to look after their loved ones competently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are currently over 40 training providers offering more than 200 Caregivers Training Grant-approved courses.

sections.label: MOH caregiver support enhancements
sections.summary: MOH has enhanced caregiver support through financial support, respite services and care navigation platforms, besides training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MOH has taken steps to enhance caregiver support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Besides training, as mentioned earlier, over the years, enhancements have been made to financial support, caregiver respite services and platforms to help with care navigation.

sections.label: Improving caregiver support and leave
sections.summary: The passage asks whether ways to improve caregiver support, such as additional caregiver leave, can be explored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we explore ways to improve caregiver support, such as offering additional caregiver leave?

sections.label: Professionalising caregiving roles
sections.summary: A scheme to professionalise caregiving is needed to formalise these roles and provide necessary training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To formalise these roles and provide the necessary training, we need to develop a scheme to professionalise caregiving.

sections.label: Falling TFR and support ratio
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR hit an all-time low of 1.05 and the old-age support ratio fell from 10.5 in 1990 to 3.8 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our TFR hit an all-time low of 1.05 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our old-age support ratio, computed as the ratio of the working-age population – meaning those 20 to 64 years old – per person aged 65 and above, has been declining, from 10.5 in 1990 to 3.8 in 2022, last year.

sections.label: Budget 2023 pro-family measures
sections.summary: Budget 2023 pro-family measures include the Baby Support Grant extension, cash support, increased Paternity Leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave, and are supportive of parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The pro-family measures announced in Budget 2023, with the Baby Support Grant extension, cash support, increased Paternity Leave and Unpaid Infant Care Leave, are, indeed, supportive of parenthood.

sections.label: Reviewing BTO programme expansion
sections.summary: COVID-19 experience shows a need to review expanding the programme to build early, before BTO flat sales, with shorter waiting time of 12 to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From our experience from COVID-19, there is a need to review to expand the programme to build early, before the sale of the BTO flats, with shorter waiting time of 12 to 18 months.

sections.label: Centres, staff and income gap
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will look into distribution of centres and staff, attracting teachers and minimising attrition, and requests a review of measures to manage the national income gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Government look into the distribution of these centres and staff, how to attract teachers into these sectors and minimise the attrition rate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to move on to request for a review of measures to manage our national income gap.

sections.label: Team motivation, meritocracy, middle-income assistance
sections.summary: A leader must motivate team members of different capabilities to work together, embrace compassionate meritocracy, and the passage appeals for more assistance for the middle-income group burdened by inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: He must be able to motivate all his team members with different capabilities and abilities to work hand in hand and care for one another as a team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We are a competitive society, but we must learn to embrace compassionate meritocracy, especially since we need to have more of the young in our workforce to support the aged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last but not least, I would like to appeal for more assistance for the middle-income group who are burdened by inflation and rising costs and yet are not qualified for most of the assistance schemes, which are targeted at lower-income groups.

sections.label: Family office fund inflows and integration
sections.summary: Inflows of funds face MAS rules on client due diligence, beneficial owners and sources of wealth; family offices bring long-term benefits but more can be done to accelerate integration and orientate them to Singapore's norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Inflows of funds are subjected to MAS' stringent rules of comprehensive client due diligence, including establishing a clear and legitimate purpose of the use of the family office structure, ascertaining the ultimate beneficial owners and corroborating the sources of wealth and funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We should welcome this inflow of family offices because they can bring many positive long-term benefits, but more can be done to accelerate their integration and contribution; and most importantly, orientate them to Singapore's norms, values and ways of working.

sections.label: WMI family office enrolments and capital
sections.summary: Since 2020 WMI has had over 1,500 enrolments for family office-related programmes, and family capital is valuable as a flexible, agile and catalytic complement to institutional capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since 2020, WMI has had over 1,500 enrolments for family office-related programmes, in testament to the strong appetite for upskilling in this area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Family capital is valuable because it can be a useful complement to institutional capital – it can be more flexible, agile and catalytic, often in line with the values of the family.

sections.label: Gap in onboarding wealthy individuals
