sections.summary: There is no systematic on-boarding process to integrate newly arrived wealthy individuals into Singapore's enterprise and investment ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: One current gap is the lack of a systematic on-boarding process to integrate newly arrived wealthy individuals into Singapore's enterprise and investment ecosystem, so they can become active members of our venture community.

sections.label: Evolving charity policies for giving
sections.summary: Charity policies must evolve to support new forms of giving, including venture philanthropy and concessionary capital to impact investing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: They aspire to tap their financial resources and networks in creative ways to make impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We must evolve our charity policies to support new forms of giving, including venture philanthropy, concessionary capital to impact investing.

sections.label: Impact Philanthropy Partnership and family offices
sections.summary: The Impact Philanthropy Partnership, led by WMI and the Private Banking Industry Group with MAS support, will help galvanise family offices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Initiatives, such as the recent launch of the Impact Philanthropy Partnership, led by WMI and the Private Banking Industry Group with the support of MAS, will help galvanise more family offices in this area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: To preserve our social compact, it is critical that they are orientated to integrate with Singapore's social norms and have the right support and access to networks, so that they can ramp up their contributions in terms of investments and impact.

sections.label: COVID-19 Budgets and future threats
sections.summary: Passing multiple Budgets through COVID-19 protected lives and livelihoods, and the House debated how to draw learnings for future threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In passing the multiple Budgets through COVID-19, we have protected lives and livelihoods, averting an economic meltdown; and even though we fared better and emerged stronger compared to many other countries, this House did not shy away from debating on how else we could have done better and how to proactively draw learnings from our experience to ready ourselves for future threats.

sections.label: GST increase and progressive system
sections.summary: The House debated the GST issue and increased the rate, using enhanced GST Vouchers and the Assurance Package to protect the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We debated this issue sensitively with maturity and empathy, and we arrived at a balanced and win-win outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And in increasing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate, we bravely acknowledged the need for fiscal sustainability and prudence to support higher and longer-term expenditures, yet effectively transformed what is a potentially regressive tax regime into a holistic and progressive system through the innovative use of enhanced GST Vouchers and the Assurance Package, so that those who are vulnerable are protected, while those who are more well-off contribute more.

sections.label: Expenditures projected to rise by 2030
sections.summary: MOF stated Singapore's expenditures will increase and are projected to rise to 20% of GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has already stated that Singapore’s expenditures will increase and is projected to rise to 20% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030.

sections.label: Workers' Party GST position
sections.summary: The Workers' Party opposes the GST increase and the overall GST system, and has offered alternatives such as spending more from the NIRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I listened carefully to the Workers’ Party’s (WP) position on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They oppose not just the GST increase but also the overall GST system, that today contributes $17 billion to our revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The WP has offered some policy alternatives, such as to spend more from our Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) framework.

sections.label: NIRC spending and future generations
sections.summary: MOF projects NIRC contributions to stay about the same share of GDP, and spending more now would leave less for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MOF has projected that NIRC contributions will be maintained at about the same percentage of GDP over the coming years; and we all know that norms in the economic and investment climate have turned to be more challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we were to spend more from the NIRC now, it must mean that we leave behind less for our next generation.

sections.label: Funding proposals without GST
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to hearing details in the coming Parliament session of how the proposals will be funded, especially without GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the coming session of Parliament, I look forward to hearing more from them the details of how the proposals will be funded, especially without GST.

sections.label: Inflation and real median incomes
sections.summary: MAS data showed core consumer prices rose 5.5% year on year in February, food prices rose over 8%, and real median incomes grew just 2% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the latest Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) data showed that core consumer prices rose by 5.5% year on year in February, with food prices up more than 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Although the MAS expects inflation to “slow more discernibly in the second half of this year” and hopefully “reach around 2.5% year on year by the end of 2023”, the projection for core consumer prices to rise by 3.5% to 4.5% over 2023 as a whole and for headline inflation to average 5.5% to 6.5% is still elevated, compared to recent history and certainly out of the comfort range for many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Real median incomes grew just 2% in 2022, almost half as fast as it used to grow in the pre-COVID-19 years.

sections.label: GDP first quarter decline
sections.summary: Singapore's GDP fell sequentially by 0.7% in the first quarter, with goods producing industries declining 4.1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Here in Singapore, gross domestic product (GDP) already fell sequentially by 0.7% in the first quarter of the year, with goods producing industries seeing a sharper 4.1% decline.

sections.label: Rising house prices and rents
sections.summary: Private residential prices rose 3.2% and HDB resale prices 0.9% in the first quarter of 2023, with both up for 12 consecutive quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: House prices have continued to climb, where, based on flash estimates for the first quarter of 2023, private residential prices rose 3.2% in the quarter while HDB resale prices rose 0.9%, with both public and private prices up for 12 consecutive quarters now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on estimates by the real estate consultancy quoted in the article, the town of Sengkang which I represent had the unfortunate honour of seeing rents rise the most across HDB estates, at 40.4% over a one-year period, with median rents now at $3,200 a month, compared to around $2,200 a month a year earlier.

sections.label: Rental housing and singles' BTO age
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates calls to expand rental housing and lower the BTO eligibility age for singles from 35 to 28.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As part of these options, I would like to once again reiterate my calls made in prior Adjournment Motions to support Singaporeans’ diverse aspirations through expanding on rental housing and to lower the BTO eligibility age for singles from 35 to 28 years old.

sections.label: Lowering singles' BTO eligibility age
sections.summary: The speaker proposes lowering singles' eligibility age for HDB BTO flats from 35 to 28 to meet younger Singaporeans' housing needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if the Government still believes in home ownership as a superior model, a pathway to ensure that younger Singaporeans’ housing needs are adequately met is to lower singles’ eligibility age for HDB BTO flats from the current 35 years to 28 years of age.

sections.label: Questions on VERS details
sections.summary: With Leon Perera and Jamus Lim, the speaker asked Sim Ann for more details about VERS at February housing Motion debates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Together with my hon friends Mr Leon Perera and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, I asked Senior Minister of State Sim Ann for more details about VERS at the housing Motion debates in February, given that we know hardly anything about it despite it being introduced about five years ago.

sections.label: WP universal sale and lease back
sections.summary: The WP proposed a universal sale and lease back scheme with HDB as buyer of last resort, exercisable by each lessee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The WP had proposed a universal sale and lease back scheme that provides a floor price for HDB resale prices where the HDB is the buyer of last resort for all lessees, where each individual lessee is empowered to exercise the scheme and not be subject to a voluntary process which is out of the hands of the individual.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance for workers
sections.summary: In Mandarin, the speaker urges the Government to roll out redundancy insurance soon to enhance workers' income security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   In view of the economic slowdown and weakening job market, I would like to urge the Government to roll out redundancy insurance for workers as soon as possible so as to enhance their income security.

sections.label: Rental flats and singles' BTO age
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates calls to expand rental flat options and lower the BTO age for singles from 35 to 28.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is even more heartening to know that MND is focusing on developing more inclusive housing options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to reiterate a call made during an earlier Adjournment Motion, which is to expand rental flat options to meet the diverse housing aspirations of Singaporeans and to lower the age requirement for single citizens to apply for BTO flats from 35 to 28 years old.

sections.label: HDB flat value and retirement
sections.summary: The passage asks whether 4G leaders will address HDB flat value declining to zero at lease end while needing to enhance value for retirement funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is this a problem that the 4G leaders plan to address?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is difficult to understand how the PAP Government will honour the promise made by the Prime Minister last month, considering the fact that the value of HDB flats will trickle down to zero when their 99-year lease ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On the other hand, we must enhance the value of HDB flats so that Singaporeans will have adequate reserve funds when they retire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, the Government needs to come up with plans as soon as possible and involve Singaporeans in the discussion.

sections.label: Respectful debates in Parliament
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker looks forward to more robust yet respectful debates, calling respectful contestation key to public trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On that note, I look forward to having more robust yet respectful debates in this House – for let us not forget that the capacity to have respectful contestation of ideas and views is a key piece in building public trust in Singapore's institutions.

sections.label: E-commerce growth in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage cites reports forecasting Singapore e-commerce sales of $19.6 billion by 2027 and growing adoption among users aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A report released by Meta and Bain & Company in September 2022 forecasted that e-commerce sales in Singapore will reach $19.6 billion by 2027, despite slower growth in 2022 caused by inflationary pressures and COVID-19-related supply chain disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A report released by Shopee Singapore in March 2023 found that there is growing adoption of e-commerce among older users, with 70% of respondents aged 55 and above indicating that they have integrated e-commerce into their daily routine.

sections.label: Mandating seller verification
sections.summary: The passage states mandating seller verification, already implemented in the US and EU, ensures seller accountability, reduces scams and aids dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Mandating seller verification, which is already being implemented in jurisdictions such as the United States (US) and the European Union (EU), will ensure accountability of sellers for their product listings, reduce scams and aid resolution of consumer disputes.

sections.label: Singapore social commerce forecast
sections.summary: The passage states some analysts expect Singapore's social commerce sector to reach more than US$1.25 billion by this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to some analysts, the social commerce sector in Singapore is expected to reach more than US$1.25 billion by this year.

sections.label: MAS PayNow phishing scam cases
sections.summary: The passage states MAS reported 610 banking-related phishing scam cases involving PayNow transactions in 2021 and the first half of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In October 2022, the MAS reported 610 cases of banking-related phishing scams involving PayNow transactions in 2021 and the first half of 2022.

sections.label: Buy Now Pay Later growth
sections.summary: WorldPay reports Buy Now, Pay Later transactions are expected to grow at a 40% compound annual rate from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a report by WorldPay, "Buy Now, Pay Later" transactions are expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 40% between 2021 and 2025.

sections.label: CASE Buy Now Pay Later safeguards
sections.summary: CASE called for safeguards including purchase limits, penalty fee limits, credit assessment and integration of spending data with credit ratings; some are in the industry Code of Conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: CASE has called for safeguards to be introduced, including limits to be set on purchases and penalty fees, credit assessment of potential users and integration of "Buy Now, Pay Later" spending data with credit ratings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Some of these proposals have been included in the industry’s Code of Conduct, which came into effect in November last year; but only some.

sections.label: Grassroots Advisors for non-ruling party constituencies
sections.summary: Non-ruling party MPs lack PA resources, and in constituencies won by non-ruling party candidates the defeated ruling party candidate becomes Grassroots Advisor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because we do not have access to the resources of the People’s Association (PA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because non-ruling party MPs who were elected to represent and serve their constituents during the general elections have been set aside in the appointment of Grassroots Advisors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The reality is, for a constituency won by a non-ruling party candidate, the defeated ruling party candidate will assume the role of the Grassroots Advisor.

sections.label: Sengkang GRC Grassroots Advisors event
sections.summary: In Sengkang GRC the appointed Grassroots Advisors are not members of any political party, yet a PAP branch chairman was invited as a guest at an Edusave awards ceremony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in the Sengkang GRC, the appointed Grassroots Advisors are not members of any political party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as shared in social media recently, a Sengkang branch chairman from the PAP was invited as a guest for the Edusave awards ceremony and took photos with the recipients and Grassroots Advisor.

sections.label: WP MPs free vote
sections.summary: The decision was made to allow each WP MP to vote on the matter as they saw fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, the decision was made to allow each WP MP to vote on the matter as they saw fit.

sections.label: Punggol East unfounded accusations
sections.summary: In the 2015 General Elections, last minute efforts spread unfounded accusations about $22.5 million in funds transferred between town councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the 2015 General Elections, there were last minute efforts during the campaigning period to spread unfounded accusations to the residents of Punggol East.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was said that the WP had failed to explain what had happened to $22.5 million worth of funds which had been transferred from Pasir Ris-Punggol Town Council to Aljunied-Hougang-Punggol East Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In summary, Sir, in a healthy democracy, the decisions of voters in electing their political representatives should be made based on their considerations on the facts that have been put forward by all parties contesting in the elections and not because of fears which had arisen from unfounded claims.

sections.label: Government COVID-19 financial aid schemes
sections.summary: The Government implemented schemes such as the temporary relief fund, COVID-19 support Grant and Job Support Scheme, and disbursed $236 million in financial aid in the year ending March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over and above, the Government's implementation of schemes such as the temporary relief fund, COVID-19 support Grant, Job Support Scheme (JSS), and the disbursement of $236 million in financial aid in its financial year ending March 2021 – there was a sense of responsibility of what we owe each other as we operate in a society.

sections.label: Emissions and net zero investment gaps
sections.summary: Researchers at a Transition Finance towards Net Zero Conference said we are 55% below the 2030 emissions reduction required and 35% below the investments required for net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In a speech last year at the Transition Finance towards Net Zero Conference, researchers highlighted that we are 55% below the emissions reduction required by 2030 and 35% below the investments required for net zero by 2050.

sections.label: Loneliness and older adults living alone
sections.summary: Ageing research in Singapore and Japan shows lonely older adults lived at least three years less and spent less of their remaining life in good health, and about 10% of Singapore residents aged 60 and above lived alone as of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, ageing research in Singapore and Japan has shown that lonely older adults not only lived at least three years less than their peers, but also spent less of their remaining life in good health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of 2020, about 10% of Singapore residents aged 60 years and above lived alone.

sections.label: Elderly suicides in 2020
sections.summary: In 2020, Singapore saw the most elderly suicides since 1991, with 154 people aged 60 and above taking their own lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Further, in 2020, in the heart of the pandemic, nationally, we saw the most number of elderly suicides since 1991 – among people aged 60 and above, a total of 154 took their own lives.

sections.label: Loneliness ministers and Singapore mental health bodies
sections.summary: Japan appointed a minister for loneliness in 2021 and the UK has had a ministerial lead since 2017, while Singapore set up an Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being in 2021 and announced an SG Mental Well-being Network in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2021, Japan appointed a minister for loneliness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The UK has had a ministerial lead on loneliness since 2017, later announcing its inaugural loneliness strategy in 2018 and a loneliness engagement fund, which provided grants between £15,000 and £50,000 to organisations, which could engage at-risk groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, in Singapore, an Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being was set up in 2021 and it was announced in 2022 that an SG Mental Well-being Network was formed, and that the establishment of a permanent National Well-being Office was being considered.

sections.label: Seniors' health and early screening
sections.summary: With average life expectancy in Singapore above 80 years, seniors should be encouraged to care for their health, adopt healthier nutrition and not fear early health screening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the average life expectancy in Singapore being above 80 years, it is important for us to look into the quality of life in our seniors’ golden years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In order to do so, we must encourage more seniors to take care of their health and incorporate healthier nutrition into their lifestyles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should raise more awareness among them that they should not be afraid to undergo early health screening because they will be able to take steps, if necessary, to take care of themselves and their loved ones.

sections.label: Leadership and difficult issues
sections.summary: It states that dialogues are held and constructive discussions welcomed, and that good leadership involves raising difficult issues and explaining merits and disadvantages before decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We hold many dialogues at various levels and welcome constructive discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, good leadership and good politics should involve a willingness to raise difficult issues and explain its merits and disadvantages before making decisions in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans based on the facts available at that time.

sections.label: Expanded Framework bilateral agreements
sections.summary: It states that President Jokowi and the speaker witnessed the signing of three bilateral agreements under an Expanded Framework: FIR, DCA and ET.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Last year, President Jokowi and I witnessed the signing of a set of three bilateral agreements under an Expanded Framework, comprising the Flight Information Region (FIR) Agreement, the Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) and the Extradition Treaty (ET).

sections.label: ICAO approval for FIR arrangements
sections.summary: It states that both governments submitted the new FIR arrangements to ICAO, and once approved, the FIR, DCA and ET agreements can come into force simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Both governments have submitted the new FIR arrangements to the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) for approval.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Once the ICAO has done so, all three agreements – FIR, DCA and ET – can come into force simultaneously.

sections.label: Singapore-Johor cooperation and RTS Link
sections.summary: It states the two countries can gain by working together in new areas like green and digital economies and on the RTS Link between Singapore and Johor Bahru.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Our two countries have much to gain by working together, both in new areas, like the green and digital economies, also on ongoing projects like the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link between Singapore and Johor Bahru.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We are building the RTS Link marine viaduct across the Straits of Johor, starting from both sides and meeting in the middle.

sections.label: Russia suspends New Start Treaty
sections.summary: It states that two months ago Russia suspended its participation in the New Start Treaty, its only remaining nuclear arms control treaty with the US.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Two months ago, Russia suspended its participation in the New Start Treaty, its only remaining nuclear arms control treaty with the US.

sections.label: US view on China competition
sections.summary: It states the prevailing American view that cooperation with China has failed, China is a grave threat, and the US must pursue extreme competition and a large lead in foundational technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The prevailing view in America is that their efforts to work out a cooperative relationship with China have failed, and China’s growing strength and assertiveness is becoming a grave threat to US interests and values.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And therefore, the US must go for “extreme competition” and maintain “as large a lead as possible”, in their words, over China, in foundational technologies such as semiconductor chips, quantum technology, artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology and green technologies – all the things that count.

sections.label: US views on China
sections.summary: A Pew survey found over 80% of US adults view China unfavourably and nearly 40% call it an enemy.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The latest Pew survey found that over 80% of adults in the US have an unfavourable view on China, and nearly 40% – four in 10 – would describe China as an enemy of the US rather than as a competitor or partner.

sections.label: China domestic issues and Taiwan
sections.summary: Hong Kong, Xinjiang and Tibet are seen as China's domestic matters, but Taiwan is the most dangerous flashpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They consider issues like Hong Kong, Xinjiang and Tibet to be China’s domestic matters, vitally affecting its security and integrity, on which they see no room for discussion or compromise.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But the most dangerous flashpoint of all is Taiwan.

sections.label: IMF global fragmentation estimate
sections.summary: The IMF estimated global economic fragmentation could cumulatively reduce global GDP by 7% in the long run.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The The International Monetary Fund (IMF) recently estimated that fragmentation of the global economy could, in the long run, reduce global gross domestic product (GDP) by 7% cumulatively.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Seven percent is a very high figure – but I think it is a conservative estimate because the reality is probably worse.

sections.label: Three simultaneous global crises
sections.summary: A hot war in Europe, superpower hostility and protectionism will disrupt the world, the region and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: A hot war in Europe, deepening hostility between two superpowers, which are closely interlinked with each other, and protectionism undermining the foundations of the multilateral trading system.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: These three simultaneous crises will set in train a whole series of changes and shocks that will severely disrupt the world, our region and surely, Singapore.

sections.label: Tudung for Muslim nurses
sections.summary: Two years ago, Muslim nurses were allowed to wear the tudung with their uniforms.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Two years ago, we allowed Muslim nurses to wear the tudung with their uniforms.

sections.label: Forward Singapore social compact
sections.summary: Forward Singapore brings Singaporeans together to refresh the social compact and create a collective roadmap.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We must nurture the deep and precious trust that we have – between the Government and people, and also among Singaporeans – and work hand-in-hand towards a shared vision of our future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: This is what Forward Singapore is about – bringing Singaporeans together to refresh our social compact and come up with a collective roadmap for our way forward.

sections.label: Government backing agenda
sections.summary: The Government will fully back this agenda with policies, programmes and resources.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: All this is absolutely essential and the Government will fully back this agenda with policies, programmes and resources.

sections.label: Rajaratnam on industrial development
sections.summary: In a 1968 Parliament speech, Rajaratnam said industrial development requires sustained effort, savings, risk-taking, innovation and postponing immediate rewards.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Speaking in Parliament at the end of the debate on the President's Address – not this debate but that debate in 1968 – he said, and I quote:	"Industrial development requires at all times a sustained effort, a willingness to mobilise savings, a readiness to take risks, a propensity for innovation, a passionate vision of the future, a willingness to make the painful adjustments required by modernisation and, most important of all, a readiness on the part of the people as a whole to postpone immediate rewards for greater gains in the future...If we are not prepared to pay this price", he said, then, there "will be little or no economic development".

sections.label: Singaporeans heeded Rajaratnam's words
sections.summary: Because Singaporeans heeded Rajaratnam's words and set their hearts and souls to nation-building, they survived the British forces' withdrawal and later crises.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Because Singaporeans heeded Mr Rajaratnam's words and set our hearts and souls to nation-building, we survived the withdrawal of the British forces, we overcame many more subsequent crises and created today's Singapore.

sections.label: Staying open and connected
sections.summary: Survival depends on doing business with the world, so the strategy must be to stay open and connected as a global city and international hub.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Our survival depends on our being able to do business with the world, to deliver value to others.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, our strategy must be to double down on staying open and connected to the world and continue making ourselves useful as a global city and an international hub.

sections.label: Singapore top among 82 countries
sections.summary: Singapore came in top among 82 countries that the EIU looked at from across the world.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Singapore came in top among 82 countries that the EIU looked at from across the world.

sections.label: EDB vaccine projects
sections.summary: The EDB has secured several vaccine projects, and Pfizer and BioNTech are separately making major investments in Singapore to produce drugs and vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The Economic Development Board (EDB) has secured several vaccine projects.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Many of us have taken their COVID-19 vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But you may not know that Pfizer and BioNTech are two companies and that both, separately, are making major investments in Singapore to produce drugs and vaccines for the global market.

sections.label: Singapore system works
sections.summary: The passage states that people know the Singapore system works and COVID-19 has made the track record stand out more.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: People know that the Singapore system works and COVID-19 has made our track record stand out even more.

sections.label: BBNJ High Seas Treaty
sections.summary: Rena was President of the negotiations for five years and last month brought parties together to conclude the BBNJ Agreement, expected to be adopted later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Rena was President of the negotiations for the last five years and, last month, she successfully brought all the parties together to conclude a new international agreement – the BBNJ Agreement or High Seas Treaty – which is expected to be adopted later this year.

sections.label: Pharma CEO investment reasons
sections.summary: The passage states a pharma CEO listed high quality people, predictable policies and a government doing the right thing as reasons to invest here.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Last week, I met the CEO of a major pharma company.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: He listed the reasons why they had decided to invest here big time – high quality people, predictable policies and a government that is doing the right thing.

sections.label: Accumulated Reserves management
sections.summary: The passage states the accumulated Reserves are well managed, well protected, earn credible returns and give a critical advantage in major crises.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Our accumulated Reserves are well managed, well protected, earn credible returns and give us a critical advantage in major crises.

sections.label: Leadership renewal support
sections.summary: The passage states the 4G Ministers chose Lawrence Wong as leader and asks for fullest support for him and the 4G Ministers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Last year, the 4G Ministers chose Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to be their leader.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I ask you to give Lawrence and the 4G Ministers your fullest support.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I ask you to give them your fullest support for now, as members of my team, but in due course when they take over the reins as the next leadership for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Help me make this leadership renewal a success for Singapore and for you.

sections.label: Citizens aged 65 and above
sections.summary: The passage states that as at June 2022, 18.4% of the citizen population are aged 65 and above, growing to 25% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As at June 2022, 18.4% of the citizen population are aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This number will grow to 25% by 2030.

sections.label: CPF retirement sum concerns
sections.summary: A member involved in CPF changes is heartened that almost 70% of active CPF members attain their cohort Basic Retirement Sum at age 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is something I am very concerned about, having previously been involved in the last round of Central Provident Fund (CPF) changes as a member of the CPF advisory panel and have advocated extensively during my Budget debate and Committee of Supply (COS) speeches on this issue this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am heartened to hear that almost 70% of active CPF members are able to attain their cohort Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) at age 55 today.

sections.label: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
sections.summary: Minister of State Gan mentioned the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme introduced in 2021 to match top-ups of up to $600 annually to eligible seniors' CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When I raised the issue of non-working homemakers at the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) COS last month, Minister of State Gan mentioned the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) introduced in 2021 to match top-ups of up to $600 annually to eligible seniors' CPF accounts.

sections.label: Support for seniors living alone
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a National Befriender Service and voluntary registration for seniors living alone, and welcomes MOH's nursing home and workforce expansion plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is time for us to enhance or embark on a National Befriender Service for Seniors Living Alone programme and maybe consider some form of voluntary registration system, perhaps using technology, for seniors living alone, so that we can check on them periodically and engage them regularly at their convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Ministry of Health’s (MOH) announcement that it will expand the capacity of our nursing homes from 16,000 beds in 2020 to more than 31,000 beds in 2030, increase the nursing workforce and caregiver support from 49,000 now to 69,000 by 2030 and increase the nursing and caregiving support workforce.

sections.label: TAFEP guidelines into law
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee announced in the National Day Rally 2021 that the Government will enshrine TAFEP guidelines into law to ensure fair workplace treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our efforts to attract and retain talent will have to be multi-pronged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I was glad to hear when Prime Minister Lee announced in the National Day Rally 2021 that the Government will be enshrining the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) guidelines into law which is a major move to ensure fair treatment at the workplace, including tackling unfair hiring practices against Singaporeans.

sections.label: Land constraints and rail network
sections.summary: Land constraints will become more acute as another 100 kilometres is added to the rail network, which already has more than 140 stations across six MRT lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our land constraints will become more acute as we add another 100 kilometres to our rail network which already has more than 140 stations across six MRT lines.

sections.label: Foreign worker framework revisions
sections.summary: Revisions to foreign worker frameworks will not eliminate labour constraints, given the need to balance local employment and attracting foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The revisions to our foreign worker frameworks will not eliminate labour constraints, given the need to strike a fine balance between keeping our local labour force gainfully employed and attracting the necessary foreign labour to supplement the local workforce.

sections.label: Credit card use and interest rates
sections.summary: The speaker notes credit cards became Singapore's most popular payment method by transaction value, amid a 3% to 4% interest rate rise between April 2022 and April 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I read in the news last week that credit cards have become the most popular payment method in Singapore by transaction value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is worrying especially given the 3% to 4% increase in interest rates just between April 2022 and April 2023.

sections.label: Affordable preschool care options
sections.summary: The speaker cites MSF's addendum that by 2025, 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool with affordable fees, and asks what metrics will price fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A key policy impetus will be ensuring that there are sufficient and affordable care options for young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)’s addendum which states that by 2025, 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool with affordable fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What metrics will the Government use to price preschool fees and keep it “affordable”?

sections.label: Report on million-dollar home affordability
sections.summary: The speaker quotes Mr Louis Chua and co-authors' report saying that despite cooling measures, a $1 million home is estimated affordable for average household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, if I may quote him, in his report, what was interesting, Mr Louis Chua and his co-authors reported and said that "despite cooling measures, a $1 million home in Singapore is estimated to be affordable for households on an overall average household income in Singapore".

sections.label: Challenges and people-government trust
sections.summary: The speaker lists ageing population, costs and interest rates, and global competition as challenges, and says maintaining people-government trust makes him optimistic about the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Before I end, Mr Speaker, our ageing population, spiralling costs and interest rates, and intensifying global competition for business and talent are just three of the major challenges we will need to target, adapt to and conquer as we stand on the cusp of a new world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have shared, I have tried to look into cost of living, housing affordability and, indeed, as Mr Desmond Lee has shared during the housing debate, we have tried to ramp up supply, we have tried to make sure we can stabilise growth in the housing sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have shared some of my points earlier on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I think what is key is that if we can maintain the same people-government trust and partnership that saw us emerge from COVID-19 much better than other countries, I am optimistic about our future.

sections.label: Poll on US-China stance
sections.summary: An MCI poll in July 2022 showed 86% of Singaporeans felt the Government should act in Singapore's best interests and not take sides between the US and China.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: A Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) poll in July 2022 showed that 86% of Singaporeans felt that their Government should always act in Singapore’s best interests and not take sides between the US and China.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Only 4% felt that Singapore should lean towards China and 4% felt that Singapore should lean towards the US.

sections.label: Singapore-China partnership upgrade
sections.summary: During the Prime Minister's Official Visit to China, Singapore and China upgraded their relationship to an All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership, covering digital and green economies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: During the Prime Minister’s Official Visit to China last month, Singapore and China upgraded our relationship to an “All‑Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership”.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This reflects both sides’ commitment to continually expand bilateral cooperation and pursue high-quality collaboration in forward-looking areas such as the digital and green economies.

sections.label: Cultural heritage and kebaya nomination
sections.summary: The Government encourages Singaporeans to appreciate cultural heritage, celebrate intermingled cultures like the kebaya, and honour their own heritage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government encourages Singaporeans to appreciate the cultural heritage of fellow Singaporeans, celebrate the products of intermingling between different cultures, such as the kebaya, which Singapore is partnering four other Southeast Asian countries in nominating for the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's (UNESCO) intangible cultural heritage list, and honour and develop their own cultural heritage.

sections.label: Chinese Singaporeans as huaren
sections.summary: Singaporeans of Chinese ethnicity are Singaporean citizens and Singapore huaren, not huaqiao.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, Singaporeans of Chinese ethnicity are very clear – they are Singaporean citizens and Singapore “huaren” (people of Chinese ethnicity), not “huaqiao” (“overseas Chinese”).

sections.label: US investment and trade
sections.summary: The US is the largest investor in Singapore and ASEAN, and Singapore's top trading partner in services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Today, the US is the largest investor in Singapore and ASEAN, and Singapore’s top trading partner in services.

sections.label: US security cooperation and MOU
sections.summary: Singapore is a Major Security Cooperation Partner of the US, supports its regional presence, and its 1990 MOU gives US military base access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore is a Major Security Cooperation Partner of the US, and we support the US military presence and its defence engagements in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), signed in 1990 and renewed recently in 2019, provides the US military with access to Singapore’s air and naval bases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore joined the US’ Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) when it was launched in May 2022.

sections.label: Honest, credible, trustworthy stance
sections.summary: Only by being honest, credible and trustworthy, not a vassal state or proxy, will Singapore's views be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Only when we persist in being honest, credible and trustworthy – not a vassal state, proxy, or stalking horse for one power or another – will our views be taken seriously.

sections.label: UN rules and BBNJ Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore participates in developing international rules at the UN, including UNCLOS and facilitating the BBNJ Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This includes participating actively in the development of international rules and norms at the United Nations (UN).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We followed up with our role in bringing about the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), adopted in 1982, by facilitating the conclusion of an international legally-binding instrument under UNCLOS on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity of areas beyond national jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) last month.

sections.label: Singapore global governance and trade
sections.summary: Singapore co-facilitated carbon market negotiations, promoted trade agreements, chaired a cybersecurity working group, and held the FATF Presidency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore co-facilitated negotiations on developing carbon markets over the past two years, thereby contributing to the world’s collective effort to limit global carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Beyond the WTO, we have also promoted inclusive economic integration through forward-looking trade agreements, such as the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) as well as Digital Economy Agreements and Green Economy Agreements with countries like Australia, Chile, New Zealand, and the UK.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore has also played an active role in norms-setting and global governance on other issues in which we have a stake.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are helping to build a secure and peaceful cyberspace through chairing the Open-ended Working Group (OEWG) on Security of and in the Use of Information and Communications Technologies 2021-2025; and contributing to the global fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism through Singapore’s Presidency of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

sections.label: Property demand-supply imbalance
sections.summary: A report for institutional investors was cited, with the key constraint described as a fundamental demand-supply imbalance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The report that he was referring to was produced for institutional investors in a commercial context for their investment decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I think if you look at the key conclusions that have been put forth in the report and what I have shared as recent as earlier this afternoon, in that the key constraint that I was speaking about is really the fundamental demand-supply imbalance issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I spoke about how demand has been resilient, BTO subscription rates, private property take-up rates have been very high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And even the number of marriages has outpaced the number of BTO flats available on the demand side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And similarly on the supply side, I also spoke about how in terms of the private property market, the number of unsold units is at an all-time low.

sections.label: Ageing Singapore population
sections.summary: By 2030, almost one in four Singaporeans will be over 65.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By 2030, almost one in four Singaporeans will be over 65.

sections.label: Digitalised CPF and LPA filing
sections.summary: CPF Board and OPG streamlined e-filing for CPF nominations and LPAs, and OPG extended its $75 LPA fee waiver to 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In recent years, we have also seen agencies, such as the CPF Board and the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), who have embraced digitalisation, streamlining the e-filing process of registering a CPF nomination and LPA respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And more recently, to appeal to the general public in ensuring that legal instruments, such as LPA, remains affordable for all, the OPG has yet again extended its $75 application fee waiver to 31 March 2026 for Singaporeans who register for LPA Form One.

sections.label: Deputy appointment without LPA
sections.summary: Without a prior LPA, family members must apply to the Family Justice Court to be appointed deputy, taking at least four to six weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Currently, if a person becomes mentally incapacitated without making a prior LPA nomination, his immediate family members will have to apply to the Family Justice Court (FJC) to be legally appointed as deputy of the incapacitated patient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A simplified process still takes at least four to six weeks or so to complete and the time	frame may be prolonged if the case gets more complex, where the Court will prompt the intended deputy to retrieve for more information.

sections.label: Reviewing Mental Capacity Act
sections.summary: A suggestion was made for the Government to review the Mental Capacity Act so certain next-of-kin can be default deputies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Aligned with what Minister Masagos has shared yesterday, that there is a need to ensure that our social services are comprehensive, convenient and coordinated so that families can get the help they need quickly and easily, to avoid going through such unnecessary hassle, I humbly suggest that the Government consider reviewing the Mental Capacity Act and recommend adjustments such that in the event where no LPA has been made, a certain category of the immediate next-of-kin can assume such responsibility to be the default deputy, upon proof to the OPG that the patient is now mentally incapacitated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This category can be aligned to what is set out in the Intestate Succession Act, where in the event that the patient is married, his or her spouse may be deemed to have the first of right to be the applicant to apply to become the deputy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the event the patient is still a bachelor when he becomes incapacitated, then either or both of his parents may be deemed to have the first of right to be his or her joint deputies unless either renounces his or her rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   As our population ages, to ensure that Singaporeans and their offspring have a peace of mind, the Government should not only educate Singaporeans about the benefits of estate planning but also delve deeper into exploring ways to assist Singaporeans in the event of unforeseen personal circumstances, for example, when a spouse suddenly suffers a stroke and is bedridden or when the sole breadwinner of the family passes away suddenly.

sections.label: Business challenges carbon tax BEPS
sections.summary: Singapore businesses face added challenges from the impending carbon tax increase and the BEPS 2.0 initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The business landscape in Singapore is facing additional challenges, including the impending increase in carbon tax and the implementation of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 initiative.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model National Productivity Fund
sections.summary: The PWM expansion and $4 billion National Productivity Fund top-up are encouraging, but effective use of funds is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The expansion of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) into other industries and the topping up of the National Productivity Fund with $4 billion is encouraging, but for the National Productivity Fund, how do we ensure the funds are effectively used to drive productivity improvements that will help lower the real cost of doing businesses?

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrator pilot rollout
sections.summary: The Jobs-Skills Integrator pilot in precision engineering, retail and wholesale trade is positive, but rollout pace is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Jobs-Skills Integrator pilot in precision engineering, retail and wholesale trade is a positive step towards this goal, but how do we speed up this pace of rollout to other industries?

sections.label: Protecting workers with skills
sections.summary: Focus should be on protecting workers and preparing them with skills rather than protecting jobs that may no longer be relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The focus should be on protecting workers and preparing them with the skills required in the evolving economy rather than protecting jobs that may no longer be relevant.

sections.label: Equality and workplace discrimination
sections.summary: TAFEP guidelines pursue equality and address workplace discrimination, but equal opportunities for seniors, persons with disabilities, special needs workers, caregivers and back-to-work mothers lag.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have also begun to pursuit at pace on equality and addressing discrimination at the workplace through our Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, we have not been as successful in providing equal opportunities for seniors, persons with disabilities, special needs workers, caregivers and back-to-work mothers.

sections.label: Grants for seniors and disabilities
sections.summary: Grants like Senior Employment Credit, Part-Time Re-Employment Grant and Uplifting Employment Credit exist, but take-up and sufficiency are questioned given ageing and disability figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While there are grants and schemes to assist with their employment such as Senior Employment Credit, Part-Time Re-Employment Grant and Uplifting Employment Credit, what is the percentage of companies that have taken up these grants?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Have we done enough, given that by 2030, 900,000 or one in four of our Singaporeans will be above the age of 65 and 3.4% of our resident population has some form of disability?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we have grants and schemes to help nudge behaviours and attitudes, we must substantially move the needle and provide equal opportunities for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is our collective societal responsibility to ensure that designing jobs for seniors, persons with disabilities, and special needs workers is our national priority.

sections.label: Disability support suggestions
sections.summary: The speaker outlines three suggestions to strengthen disability support, particularly in the post-18 space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With these thoughts in mind, I outline today three suggestions to strengthen disability support, particularly in the post-18 space.

sections.label: Post-18 case coordination gap
sections.summary: MSF and MOE have tightened transitions, but case coordination for persons with disabilities in post-18 years needs strengthening, as centre-based services leave gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Whilst the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Ministry of Education (MOE) have done much to tighten transitions from early intervention to the schooling years, and from the schooling years into the community, there is a need to strengthen case coordination services to support persons with disabilities (PwDs) throughout their post-18 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Today, our post-18 services, such as Day Activity Centres, are centre-based.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This means that persons with disabilities who do not quite fit into any of the existing service models fall into a service gap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Also, the centre-based approach, as opposed to a person-centric approach, places the burden of sourcing for the right service squarely on the shoulders of the persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Hence, if a person with disabilities does not join any post-18 centre-based services after their schooling years, they also cease to receive much needed case management support.

sections.label: Integrated social-health support
sections.summary: The third point is the provision of integrated, social-health support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Third is the provision of integrated, social-health support.

sections.label: MediFund coverage for Adult Disability Homes
sections.summary: MediFund provides a safety net for patients with medical bill difficulties, and the speaker asks about extending its coverage to Adult Disability Homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For example, MediFund provides a safety net for patients who face difficulties with remaining medical bills after receiving Government subsidies and drawing on other means of payment, including those who need intermediate and long-term care in facilities, such as nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Can we consider extending its coverage to Adult Disability Homes which also provide long-term care?

sections.label: Implementing EMP2030 and inclusive Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says more must be done, including implementing EMP2030 and building a caring, inclusive Singapore supporting persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But there is also consensus that there is much more we can, and must do, including in the areas I have highlighted today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We must push ahead with our ongoing efforts to implement EMP2030 and forge a more caring and inclusive Singapore where including and supporting PwDs is part of our everyday lives, where inclusive businesses and services are the norm in our communities, and where PwDs have access to the opportunities and support they need to pursue their aspirations and realise their fullest potential in their everyday lives, just as anyone else would.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I duly recognise the report is meant for institutional clients as he mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: But the professional assessment and conclusion in the report is very explicit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Public housing in Singapore today remains affordable, I think I have highlighted the quotes just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I am glad that Mr Chua agrees with us on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I just want to reiterate that if he looks at the report, the key conclusion there really is that the key issue which I highlighted consistently across, is that it is really a matter of demand and supply, and what may be favourable from an investment perspective may not exactly be favourable from a national interest perspective.

sections.label: Chua report on housing affordability
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Chua's report explicitly states public housing in Singapore is affordable and welcomes his agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The bottom line is that Mr Chua's report explicitly states public housing in Singapore is affordable and that in Mr Chua's professional assessment, we are glad to have his agreement on this matter.

sections.label: Work from home and annual leave
sections.summary: The speaker repeats calls to legislate the right to work from home and to increase the minimum annual leave entitlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, I repeat my calls to legislate the right to work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, I repeat my calls to increase the minimum amount of annual leave entitlement.

sections.label: COVID-19 work from home legislation
sections.summary: When COVID-19 hit, work from home was legislated and made compulsory for most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When COVID-19 hit, we legislated and made work from home compulsory for most.

sections.label: Legislate right to work from home
sections.summary: The speaker suggests legislating the right to work from home and giving people the choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first suggestion is that we legislate the right to work from home and give people the choice.

sections.label: Increase minimum annual leave
sections.summary: The speaker says people should be given more rest and the minimum annual leave increased, calling the current seven days extremely low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, we should also give our people more time to rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should increase the minimum amount of annual leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The current minimum of only seven days of annual leave is extremely low.

sections.label: Breastfeeding mothers workplace discrimination
sections.summary: The speaker suggests ensuring the proposed workplace discrimination law covers discrimination breastfeeding mothers face at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first suggestion is for breastfeeding mothers and that we ensure the proposed workplace discrimination law will also cover the discrimination breastfeeding mothers face at work.

sections.label: Review policies for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a whole-of-Government review to ensure policies are inclusive for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second suggestion is for single unwed parents and that we do a whole-of-Government review to ensure our policies are inclusive for single unwed parents.

sections.label: Stigma against single unwed parents
sections.summary: The speaker says policy changes have been made for inclusiveness but more is needed to tackle stigma and discrimination facing single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have seen how we can make changes to our policies in the spirit of inclusiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But again, there is more that needs to be done to tackle the stigma and discrimination that still persists for many single unwed parents.

sections.label: Fair policies for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a review of policies so single unwed parents and their children have equal opportunities, and supports the Motion of Thanks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Single unwed parents are just trying their best for their children in difficult circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope again that we will review our policies to ensure that they are inclusive and fair for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are not asking to incentivise being a single unwed parent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are asking that we provide them a level and equal playing field so that they and their children can have equal opportunities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I will continue to speak up because our lives begin to end the day we become silent about issues that matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support the Motion of Thanks to the President.

sections.label: Challenges of an ageing population
sections.summary: The passage states that by 2030 one in four will be above 65, bringing challenges such as healthcare demand, costs, a shrinking workforce, social services, retirement funding, ageism and isolation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2010, one in 10 were above 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: By 2030, it will be one in four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As our population ages, we will face several challenges, such as increased demand for healthcare services, rising healthcare costs, a shrinking workforce, increased demand for social services, retirement funding, ageism and social isolation.

sections.label: Forward Singapore social compact exercise
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore exercise is described as how values and priorities are collectively explored and the social compact strengthened for the nation's next bound.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Forward Singapore exercise is how we collectively explore our values and priorities and strengthen our social compact for the next bound of our nation's journey.

sections.label: Opportunities and pressures for youths
sections.summary: The passage states the wish to give youths opportunities to reach their fullest potential and describes the values, identity and challenges faced by various groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: To the youths, we want to give our youths opportunities to expand and live to their fullest potential, unbridled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our youths must have the determination, ambition, passion and, more importantly, be centred on a strong set of values, identity and culture, to have that curiosity and eagerness for adventure, not just to travel, but to explore new worlds and domains, to build expertise and develop networks and, at every step, be an ambassador of Singapore that values identity and culture – to be proud of being Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: To those doing their level best, those with elderly parents, young children, a family member with chronic illnesses or disabilities and those facing pressures and hostile workplaces, to those who had and needed second chances in life, there are days when you feel alone, facing insurmountable challenges.

sections.label: Building pathways for future generations
sections.summary: The passage states that pathways will be built today to propel future generations forward with greater strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: For our future generations, we shall build the pathways today that will propel us forward with greater strength.

sections.label: Pro-family policies and fertility rate
sections.summary: Pro-family policies continue even as the total fertility rate fell to an all-time low of 1.05 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For many decades, our policies have been pro-family and increasingly so over the past few years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These policies are not slowing down even though our total fertility rate continues to plunge year after year, hitting an all-time low of 1.05 in 2022.

sections.label: Required leave types in Singapore
sections.summary: Companies must provide maternity, paternity, childcare and unpaid infant care leave, but not family, parent or eldercare leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Companies in Singapore are required to provide maternity, paternity, childcare and unpaid infant care leave, but not family, parent or eldercare leave.

sections.label: Call for medical and caregiving leave
sections.summary: A call for the Government to consider mandatory medical appointments leave and caregiving leave for all employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: (In English): I would like to call upon the Government to consider some medical appointments leave and caregiving leave for parents, to be a mandatory benefit for all employees.

sections.label: Isolation and seniors found dead
sections.summary: Isolation is not a good option as social interaction is essential, and news reports of seniors found dead alone at home are no longer uncommon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But living in isolation is not a good option and social interaction is essential for one’s cognitive and physical health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These days, sadly, it is no longer uncommon for news reports of seniors found dead alone at home.

sections.label: Co-living for seniors in HDB flats
sections.summary: A call for HDB to lease existing flats in mature estates to set up co-living options for singles, divorced and widowed Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The problems of seniors living in isolation will not be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I like to call for HDB to consider leasing out some of the existing HDB flats in mature estates where the seniors are familiar with and are served by nearby neighbourhood amenities, to set up co-living options for singles, divorced and widowed Singaporeans.

sections.label: Trust arrangements for elderly scam victims
sections.summary: A call for the Government to set up trust arrangements for the elderly, especially singles without partners or children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Recent scams via phones and online sites had depleted the bank accounts of many senior citizens, even those who are highly educated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I strongly urge the Government to set up trust arrangements for the elderly, especially for singles who do not have partners nor children to help them.

sections.label: CPF financial services for retirees
sections.summary: Speaker urges CPF to consider offering financial services so retirees' funds can be managed by trusts paying expenses and monthly pocket money.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Their funds can be managed by the trusts which will pay for their expenses such as medical bills and release their pocket money monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I urge CPF to consider offering such financial services to retirees, especially to single seniors, so that their retirement funds can be well-managed and protected.

sections.label: Services for bequeathing to charities
sections.summary: Speaker urges MSF and VWOs to set up services helping people bequeath assets to charitable organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
