sentences.text: Perhaps they may have assets that they wish to bequeath to charitable organisations but are not familiar with the arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and volunteer welfare organisations (VWOs) to look into setting up such services to assist them, so that they can leave the world with a peace of mind.

sections.label: Residents sign up, suicide data
sections.summary: Over 600 residents above 40 signed up two months into operations, and 378 people took their own lives in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two months into operations, more than 600 residents above 40 years old have signed up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the data from the Samaritans of Singapore, a non-religious and not-for-profit charity focusing on crisis intervention and suicide prevention, 378 people here took their own lives in 2021, with the largest group aged 10 to 29 years old.

sections.label: Speeding up mental health treatments
sections.summary: Speaker urges Government to speed up mental health treatments and support, starting with more training and subsidies for family doctors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to urge the Government to speed up augmenting mental health treatments and support, currently mostly delivered through hospital psychiatric wards by specialists like psychiatrists or psychologists, in three ways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, by providing more training and subsidies to family doctors in GP clinics, to make them the first line of care for mental health.

sections.label: Mentoring scheme and ABCN platform
sections.summary: Speaker partnered NTUC Women and Family Division to widen mentors through the Women-Supporting-Women Mentoring Scheme, and describes ABCN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In my constituency, I have partnered the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Women and Family Division to widen the pool of mentors through the Women-Supporting-Women Mentoring Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: ABCN is a purpose-led, not-for-profit platform established by a group of like-minded CEOs who collaborate to maximise their impact, especially in making a difference to kids facing poverty, violence or drugs.

sections.label: Fertility rate and parenthood survey
sections.summary: Total fertility rate hit a record low, and the 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey cites stress and work-family demands besides financial costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our total fertility rate has hit record low last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has done a lot in increasing financial incentives like raising the Baby Bonus, the subsidies for assistive reproduction procedures, infant care and childcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These are all important measures but according to the 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey, besides financial costs, stress and difficulties in managing work and family demands remain the other top reasons why Singaporeans are not prepared to have more children.

sections.label: GP mental health training
sections.summary: Family doctors need continuous training, peer consultations, longer consultations and higher subsidies to treat common mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For most of the children, youths and adults facing mental health issues at the early stage, it would be less stressful for them to walk into a GP clinic than to go to a psychiatric ward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Most family doctors would have received some basic training, but as common mental health conditions, like depression and anxiety, are harder to treat than coughs and colds, many family doctors need continuous education and training, as well as peer-consultations opportunities from their peers and specialists, and collaboration with counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Consultations will also take a longer time and they will need higher subsidies for consultation with patients struggling with mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to an IPS survey on "Future of Work Singaporeans Want" in October 2022, young Singaporeans prioritise personal growth, learning opportunities and career progression over job security.

sections.label: Unpaid labour recognition
sections.summary: The WP manifesto calls for greater recognition of unpaid labour, and the speaker had asked for time-use surveys in national statistics.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On our invisible, unpaid workers, the Workers' Party (WP) manifesto calls for greater recognition of unpaid labour, as a first step to develop policies that guard against these essential workers ending up with a lack of resources and even becoming indigent in what should be their golden years.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my maiden speech in 2020, I had called for quantification of the work done by these workers, asking for time-use surveys to be a part of our national statistics system.

sections.label: Warming effect on workers
sections.summary: The disproportionate effect of a warming world on blue collar manual workers and vulnerable households needs to be better understood and addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The disproportionate effect that a warming world has on blue collar manual workers and also our more vulnerable households, needs to be better understood and addressed and this is particularly urgent, given last week's logging of a temperature of 36.1°C in Woodlands.

sections.label: Whistle-blower protections proposal
sections.summary: His proposals include whistle-blower protections to ensure confidentiality for workers calling out unsafe practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: His proposals include better protection to allow workers to feel more comfortable in calling out unsafe practices by instituting whistle-blower protections to ensure confidentiality for such complaints.

sections.label: Quantifying business cost
sections.summary: He hopes the cost can be quantified as an absolute number and as a percentage of total construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To address concerns about adding to the business cost, I hope that we can properly quantify what cost this would entail, both as an absolute number across the industry and as a percentage of total construction costs, as a first step to find effective solutions to replace this outdated practice.

sections.label: Workplace anti-discrimination legislation
sections.summary: The interim report proposes new prohibited grounds of discrimination but does not prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With the Milieu Insight report last year finding that one in two workers in Singapore experienced workplace discrimination in the last five years, the enactment of anti-discrimination legislation for the workplace cannot come soon enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, while the interim report proposes new prohibited grounds of discrimination such as nationality, pregnancy status, mental health conditions, on top of existing TAFEP grounds of age, race, gender, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, it does not prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.

sections.label: Denial of reasonable accommodations
sections.summary: The denial of reasonable accommodations should fall within the meaning of discrimination in the new legislation, in line with global best practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In addition, in line with best practices around the world, the denial of reasonable accommodations should also fall within the meaning of "discrimination" in the new legislation.

sections.label: Disabled workers not reporting discrimination
sections.summary: The Disabled People's Association noted many disabled workers do not report discrimination because reporting channels are not accessible to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As the Disabled People's Association noted in their response to the interim report, many disabled workers do not report the discrimination they face because the reporting channels are themselves not accessible to them.

sections.label: UN call for anti-discrimination laws
sections.summary: In December 2022, the UN called on member states to enact comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation going beyond the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In December 2022, the UN called on member states to enact comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation which goes beyond the workplace.

sections.label: Proposed Freedom of Information Act
sections.summary: The Manifesto proposes a Freedom of Information Act with exceptions for national security and defence, serving public interest through transparency.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this regard, our Manifesto contains a proposal for a Freedom of Information Act to be enacted, with exceptions for matters relating to national security and defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having more information in the public domain leads to a more informed society and builds a democracy where citizens are exposed to all shades of opinion, because public interest is served through enhanced transparency and where communities are best able to make informed choices.

sections.label: Building trust for unity in diversity
sections.summary: The next lap for Team Singapore is building mutual trust between Government and people as a foundation for unity in diversity.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The next lap for Team Singapore then is how to continue to build mutual trust between the Government and the people in a world that changes ever more rapidly, and how to keep working on this trust as a strong foundation to fulfil our ultimate aim of unity in diversity.

sections.label: MOF cohort education outcomes
sections.summary: MOF's report on socioeconomic outcomes shows 32% of the Merdeka Generation and 49% of seniors born 1960-1969 progressed beyond secondary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) report on key socioeconomic outcomes across cohorts, 32% of the Merdeka Generation cohort progressed beyond secondary education, while 49% of seniors born between 1960 and 1969 made it there.

sections.label: Social networks and older men
sections.summary: A 2010 Singapore study found strong social networks outside the household moderated depressive symptoms among older men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A 2010 study on older men and women in Singapore found that having a strong social network outside of the household moderated depressive symptoms among older men.

sections.label: SACs and male under-representation
sections.summary: A 2011 study found men under-represented among frequent SAC users, and at Fei Yue Seniors Activity Centre female participation was three times higher than male.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As of 2019, there are more than 50 SACs serving approximately 40,000 seniors in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, a 2011 study on social networks and depressive symptoms among older adults in Singapore revealed that men, 40%, are under-represented, as compared to women, 60%, among frequent users of SACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the Fei Yue Seniors Activity Centre at Zhenghua where I serve as a Member of Parliament, the current membership of females is 56.8%, while for males it is 43.2%, roughly equal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, the participation rate for females are three times higher than males: 75.8% for females and 24.2% for males.

sections.label: Senior employment workplace policies
sections.summary: The Government initiated inclusive workplace policies including the Senior Employment Credit and Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Government has initiated inclusive workplace policies such as the Senior Employment Credit where wage offsets are provided for employers who hire seniors aged 55 and above and other policies like the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant.

sections.label: CareersFinder availability for seniors
sections.summary: MOM shared CareersFinder helps employees at any career stage, and it was asked whether it is available to seniors beyond retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Notably, in the recent Ministry of Manpower (MOM) Committee of Supply (COS), MOM shared about CareersFinder being a viable resource to help employees climb the career ladder, stay current and employable, regardless of whether one is in their early, mid or later stage of his or her career.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Will the CareersFinder through the Jobs Transformation Maps (JTMs) be available to seniors beyond the official retirement age?

sections.label: WHO age-friendly cities framework
sections.summary: Age-friendly civic participation and employment is a crucial domain in the World Health Organization's framework for age-friendly cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Age-friendly civic participation and employment is a crucial domain in the World Health Organization's framework for age-friendly cities.

sections.label: Stages of civic engagement process
sections.summary: The civic engagement process has four stages, but engagements with older adults may be limited to informing and consulting rather than partnership or ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The civic engagement process encompasses four stages: informing, consulting, partnership and complete ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, due to the challenges mentioned above, engagements with older adults may be limited to informing and consulting, rather than involving them in partnership or complete ownership of decision-making processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As shared earlier in my speech, the new cohort of seniors will lead healthier lives through Healthier SG and with more focused engagements for key demographics such as men and more formal employment and volunteering opportunities, our seniors will be able to take part fully in the civic participation process.

sections.label: GUSTO study findings
sections.summary: The findings in the Growing Up In Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes, GUSTO study, had been informative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The findings in the Growing Up In Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes, GUSTO study, had been informative.

sections.label: Youth mentoring efforts
sections.summary: In 2021 the Mentoring Alliance for Action was set up, followed a year later by Mentoring SG, while M3 oversees youth mentoring and empowerment in the Malay/Muslim space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2021, the Mentoring Alliance for Action was set up to develop common resources and share best practices on mentoring to raise the standards of mentoring in the youth sector and help young people achieve their full potential.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A year later, an independent office, Mentoring SG was set up to continue building on this effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In the Malay/Muslim space, I oversee the youth mentoring and empowerment efforts in M3, aimed at making mentoring programmes available and accessible to our young people.

sections.label: Building capability and culture
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that some attention be given to build two areas, capability and culture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As we call for more stakeholders to play a role, I would like to propose that some attention be given to build two areas – capability and culture.

sections.label: Volunteer training and development
sections.summary: Volunteers are expected to engage families or individuals and give guidance on Government resources, and a strategic approach is needed for growing and sustaining the volunteer pool.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: They do not just arrange tables and chairs but are expected to engage families or individuals with challenges or give guidance on existing Government resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I note that often training is provided before the volunteers are brought on board a certain programme but it is imperative, that we take a strategic approach in growing the volunteer pool, maintaining the interest, tapping on existing volunteer groups, rationalising the competing needs in various sectors for volunteers and having a sustainable volunteer development path.

sections.label: Target group needs and collaboration
sections.summary: The passage asks what the target group needs and suggests collaborating on an existing effective programme instead of always having new programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: What is the need of your target group and what can be done to make more impactful changes?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We do not always need to have new programmes but maybe we could collaborate on an existing programme so that we can strengthen that programme, if it is effective.

sections.label: Employer employee relationship
sections.summary: The passage states the employer-employee relationship is a two-way street and urges employers to make flexible work arrangements a permanent feature of the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The relationship between the employer and employee is a two-way street.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I would assert that there is a lot more that employers can do in taking the responsibility to create a positive and thriving work environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Have frank conversations about expectations, respect needs and aspirations of your staff, explore creative solutions and arrangements that can be a win-win for your team.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have learnt some lessons during the pandemic, for example, on the value and feasibility of flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I urge more employers to press on and make FWAs a permanent feature of the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Doing so may require adjustments to be made to your businesses and HR practices, possibly also to the way work is configured so that the load can be effectively and flexibly shared.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: However, I believe this can result in improved productivity.

sections.label: Youths from modest and middle-class backgrounds
sections.summary: The first group are youths from very modest backgrounds, a small group, and the second are middle-class youths who have done very well, a larger group whose ambition to succeed can be preserved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The first group are youths from very modest backgrounds, a very small group, and the second group are youths from the middle class who have done very well, and this is a larger group for whom we can do more to preserve their ambition to succeed.

sections.label: HDB cash flow and downpayment help
sections.summary: The speaker hopes HDB can consider helping these youths with cash flow by allowing them to pay only half the downpayment and increasing their loan quantum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: First, I hope the Housing and Development Board (HDB) can consider helping them with their cash flow by allowing them to pay only half the downpayment and increasing the loan quantum that they can enjoy.

sections.label: Career mentoring and peer support
sections.summary: The speaker says these youths can also be better supported with career mentoring and peer support outside the traditional school environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Second, we can also better support these youths with career mentoring and peer support outside of the traditional school environment.

sections.label: MOE teaching life skills
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry of Education can consider teaching youths more life skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I hope that the Ministry of Education (MOE) can consider teaching our youths more life skills.

sections.label: Raising BTO income ceiling
sections.summary: The speaker hopes HDB can consider raising the income ceiling for BTOs over time and locking the income criteria to within three years of successful booking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To address this issue, I hope that HDB can consider, over time, raising the income ceiling for BTOs and also locking the income criteria to within three years of successful booking of the flat.

sections.label: HDB backlog, Forward Singapore, condominium prices
sections.summary: The speaker notes HDB's priority is completing the flat backlog, hopes the Government signals its intention after Forward Singapore, and considers measures to moderate condominium prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I understand that HDB's current priority must be to complete the existing backlog of flats, and relaxing the application criteria now would only lengthen the waiting time for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: However, if the Government intends to adjust this sometime later, after the housing shortage is resolved, I hope that the Government can signal its intention after the completion of Forward Singapore to reduce anxiety and moderate housing demand for this group of youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Additionally, I hope the Government can also consider more measures to moderate condominium prices, particularly in non-city core areas by non-Singaporeans.

sections.label: Future plans and unity
sections.summary: The speaker urges sharing future plans and persuading people that resources and creativity can achieve them despite troubled times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Let us share with them our future plans and persuade them that we have the resources and creativity to achieve these despite the troubled times and convince them that if we preserve the spirit of personal responsibility, if we maintain good governance and internal unity, if we support one another in good times and bad, there is a world of possibilities for them and for Singapore.

sections.label: UN ageing definitions
sections.summary: The UN defines a country as ageing at 7% aged 65 or older, aged above 14%, and super-aged at 21%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The United Nations (UN) defines a country as "ageing" if the share of its population aged 65 years or older crosses 7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, magic number 7% means you are ageing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is considered "aged" if the share exceeds 14%, and once that share reaches 21%, it is considered "super-aged".

sections.label: Singapore ageing timeline
sections.summary: Singapore's gap between aged and super-aged is estimated at nine years, reaching super-aged status in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One hundred and fifteen years, 85 years, 69 years – and we, 19 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And then the gap for Singapore between "aged" and "super-aged" is estimated at only nine years, which means we will attain "super-aged" status in 2026.

sections.label: France pension deficit
sections.summary: France has projected a pension system deficit of 10 billion Euros a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: France has projected a pension system deficit of 10 billion Euros a year.

sections.label: HDB improvement programmes
sections.summary: HDB selected over 300,000 flats built up to 1986 for HIP and expanded EASE with ramps and wheelchair lifters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the flat level, HDB has selected more than 300,000 flats built up to 1986, for the Home Improvement Programme (HIP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: HDB has also announced earlier this month that the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme will be expanded to include more features, such as customised ramps and wheelchair lifters.

sections.label: Growth rate decline

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Between 2002 and 2012, it grew by 30%; but in the next decade, it only grew by 15%.

sections.label: Senior labour force participation

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The labour force participation rate for resident seniors aged 65 and above has almost tripled over the last two decades, and it is about 32% now.

sections.label: CPF LIFE, Workfare, Silver Support
sections.summary: CPF LIFE was introduced in 2009, Workfare in 2007 and Silver Support in 2016 to address retirement savings challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, those who live longer may see their CPF savings run out before they pass on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, in 2009, we introduced the CPF LIFE scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singaporeans turning 65 in 2023 who meet a stipulated level of savings in their CPF accounts are automatically enrolled in CPF LIFE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Another challenge is that some segments of society do not save enough in their CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, in 2007, we introduced Workfare, to top up the salaries of lower-income workers so that they can save more for retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2016, we implemented the Silver Support Scheme, which provides cash support for seniors who have accumulated less retirement savings in their working years.

sections.label: Healthier SG preventive care strategy
sections.summary: Building on a foundation established over many years, Healthier SG, a preventive care strategy, will launch in July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Worse, it can cripple the finances of governments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, building on the foundation established over many years, we developed Healthier SG, our preventive care strategy which we will launch in July this year.

sections.label: Social factors determine health

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Studies show that 60% of health is determined by social factors, within communities and families.

sections.label: Community care as MOH priority
sections.summary: Beyond Healthier SG, MOH's next major priority is to build up community care to support ageing in communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And this is the next area where big changes need to take place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, beyond Healthier SG, the next major area of priority for the Ministry of Health (MOH), is to build up community care, to get us all to do what is right for our health, to support ageing in communities.

sections.label: Government support for individual health
sections.summary: The Government will provide the support and structure for individuals to take care of their own health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Government will provide the support and structure for individuals to take care of their own health.

sections.label: WP and GST support

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Because to do more, one has to spend more, and one has to say where the money is coming from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: However, the WP never supported the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system.

sections.label: WP NIRC formula proposal

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it has changed its long-held position and now accepts that GST is needed, but merely objects to the increase from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Then to make up for the loss of two percentage point of GST revenue, the WP has proposed, amongst other things, changes to the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) formula.

sentences.text: So, instead of drawing half of NIRC for Government spending, WP proposes to draw a higher amount or a higher percentage at 60%.

sections.summary: The current formula deliberately divides the NIRC equally, half for current spending and half for future savings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To achieve this, the current formula is deliberately designed to divide the NIRC equally – half for current generation to spend and the other half adds to the savings for the future.

sections.label: Finland happiness ranking
sections.summary: Finland was ranked happiest country six years in a row, with Finns happy about their social safety net but worried about security and politics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Another interesting fact about Finland is that the World Happiness Report ranked the Finns as the happiest people in the world, six years in a row.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The report says the Finnish people are happy about their strong social safety net, but they also worry a lot about their security and domestic political situation.

sections.label: Singapore super-aged society
sections.summary: Singapore has a quiet unity and optimism to overcome challenges, and being a super-aged society could ultimately be good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But for Singapore, a small island along the equator, in the middle of Southeast Asia with a diverse population at the intersection of the world, I think we have a different trait, a quiet unity, optimism and stout heartedness that we can together, overcome all challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But perhaps the state of being a "super-aged" society can ultimately and overall be a good thing too – where people live long fruitful lives; where there is health, longevity; where there is warmth and care in every community, and we look out for each other.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And perhaps one day, after we tackle the challenges of a "super-aged "society with our Singapore spirit, we can reach the stage where society treats age as nothing but a number and 65 need not be that artificial line that divides the two sides of the dependency ratio.

sections.label: Fifty-fifty NIRC apportionment
sections.summary: The speaker expresses the view that the balance is best struck at 50-50 with equal apportionment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And, of course, Deputy Prime Minister Wong is the Finance Minister, but I am expressing my view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think the balance is best struck when it is 50-50, with equal apportionment.

sections.label: Honouring half-half in Constitution
sections.summary: The passage says honouring "half-half" is a matter of values and principles now in the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It was not a lesson in reducing the growth of meat consumption for the long term but it is about how we preserve peace and sometimes, 50-50 is the best and the most wise way of doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is a matter of values, principles, for future generations that are not born, we should honour "half-half" and it is in our Constitution now.

sections.label: GST 7% accepted, hike opposed
sections.summary: The position is to accept GST at 7% but oppose the hike to 8% and 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: My response to the question is that if you go back to the debates in this House that we have had about the GST hike from 7% to 9% and the positions we laid out, the position that we have adopted, at least from that time, which I believe was 2018, is that we accept the reality of a GST at 7%, because the amount of revenue that is generated by a 7% GST is so substantial and has become such a structural part of the Government revenue mix, that to want to bring that down to zero would involve too many other trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, we do accept that the GST at 7% is something that we do not oppose, but we oppose the hike to 8% and 9%.

sections.label: Difference over 2%-point GST
sections.summary: The difference between the parties is the 2%-points in GST and how it is made up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But I think some of our Members may also expand on this subsequently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the difference between us is the 2%-points in GST and how you make up for it.

sections.label: Foreign manpower growth and COMPASS
sections.summary: A concern was raised that foreign manpower from one nationality grew faster, and COMPASS now includes nationality as a criterion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the debate on the Motion on foreign talent policy, what we did was to point out that the growth rate of foreign manpower from a particular nationality is growing at a much faster rate than other nationalities, and that is factual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And so, today, we have COMPASS, which includes nationality as one of the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I think that is recognition that this is a valid concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I just want to specify that it was never a matter of race.

sections.label: Financing proposals and BTO supply
sections.summary: Financing proposals generating about $3 billion to $3.5 billion would address the GST shortfall, and the housing paper did not propose cutting BTO supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But I think that it is clear that we have offered differentiated alternative policies and I cited a number of examples in my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, now that I have clarified that we are talking about – assuming that we have 7% GST in the revenue mix but opposing an increase to 9% – I would point out again that the financing proposals we have put forward in the past, which would generate approximately $3 billion to $3.5 billion in incremental revenue, would address that GST shortfall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: We have explained it multiple times in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And the last point I make is on the reference to the housing paper that the WP put up in 2019, we did not actually propose a cutback in BTO supply or halting BTO supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The proposal that we put forward was that BTO supply and construction should continue, but should taper down when flats start to hit year 70, because we had a very specific proposal on what can be done when flats hit year 70.

sections.label: Fundamental differences and NIRC
sections.summary: The passage says fundamental differences matter most to Singaporeans, including on NIRC, involving value and belief systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But I think what matters most to Singaporeans in deciding between the parties are the fundamental differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And here, I think there is one, when it comes to NIRC, because value systems and belief systems are involved.

sections.label: Paris Agreement and climate impacts
sections.summary: The Paris Agreement committed to capping warming at 1.5°C, but cumulative greenhouse gases already harm ecosystems, temperatures, sea levels, weather, food and disease risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Paris Agreement signalled a global commitment to cap global warming to 1.5°C and there is a clear need for the world to act fast to reduce emission quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Even so, the cumulative greenhouse gases in the atmosphere have already created deep and lasting impacts on our ecosystems, raising temperatures and sea levels, increasing the frequency of extreme weather events, disrupting food production and exacerbating the risk of infectious diseases.

sections.label: Consumption depletes resources and landfill
sections.summary: Consumption depletes scarce resources, burdens the environment with waste, and exhausts space in Singapore's only Semakau landfill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It depletes our planet's scarce resources and burdens our environment with the waste that it generates, often degrading the surroundings that we share with other living creatures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: And as we consume more and dispose more in Singapore, we exhaust the finite space left in our one and only Semakau landfill.

sections.label: Social compact guides sustainable development
sections.summary: The social compact guides Singapore's sustainable development model through the colossal change of climate action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In charting our model of sustainable development going forward, our social compact is our guiding light as we navigate the colossal change that climate action entails.

sections.label: Government environmental policies and measures
sections.summary: The Government introduces policies including the Extended Producer Responsibility framework, a disposable carrier bag charge and a Beverage Container Return Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government introduce policies such as the Extended Producer Responsibility framework and measures like the disposable carrier bag charge and Beverage Container Return Scheme.

sections.label: Tampines food waste digestor
sections.summary: Tampines community, funded by NEA, installed a food waste digestor; retailers segregate food waste, cutting waste collector trips, incinerator waste and carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Another example, the community in Tampines, with funding support from the National Environment Agency (NEA), installed a food waste digestor that converts food waste into compost and nutrients for vegetable farming and landscaping.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Food retailers in the neighbourhood, such as wet market merchants and supermarkets, segregate food waste for the digestor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This cuts down the resources needed for disposal: reducing the number of trips made by waste collectors from four to one per day; decreasing the amount of waste sent to the incinerators by 400 kilogrammes every day; and saving the carbon emission from waste treatment.

sections.label: Singapore land below sea level
sections.summary: About 30% of Singapore's land area is less than five metres above mean sea level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: About 30% of our land area is less than five metres above mean sea level.

sections.label: Sea level protection cost
sections.summary: At the 2019 National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee said around $100 billion or more may be needed to protect Singapore against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: At the 2019 National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee said that around $100 billion or more may be required to protect Singapore against rising sea levels.

sections.label: Coastal protection research programmes
sections.summary: A $125 million Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme supports solutions, and the Centre for Climate Research Singapore, set up in 2013, models climate change effects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Even as we work out and implement our adaptation solutions, we will need the capabilities and knowledge to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We have a $125 million Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme (CFRP) to support the development of innovative coastal protection and flood management solutions, and we established the Centre for Climate Research Singapore (CCRS) earlier in 2013, 10 years ago, to understand the science of climate change and to model its effects, as the basis of our climate adaptation efforts.

sections.label: 30 by 30 food goal
sections.summary: Mega trends like climate change, geopolitical tensions and disease outbreaks pressure food sources, so Singapore set a goal to produce 30% of nutritional needs locally by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: However, if we look beyond the immediate term, we see the mega trends of climate change and extreme weather events, geopolitical tensions and disease outbreaks that will cause volatility to food production and place increasing pressure on our food sources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This is why we have set our "30 by 30" goal – to have the capability and capacity to produce 30% of our nutritional needs locally by 2030.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang agri-food cluster
sections.summary: The Government will support farms and set the stage through infrastructure like the Lim Chu Kang Masterplan, transforming the area into a high-tech, productive, resource-efficient agri-food cluster.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government will do our part to support and enable our farms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will set the stage through infrastructure developments like the Lim Chu Kang Masterplan (LCKMP), which will transform the area into a high-tech, highly productive and resource-efficient agri-food cluster.

sections.label: Long-term planning and environmental stewardship
sections.summary: Amid resource constraints and climate change, Singapore is not helpless, requiring grit, environmental stewardship alongside growth, infrastructure investment and difficult trade-offs, turning challenges into strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Even as we live in an increasingly uncertain and disrupted world, characterised by resource constraints and climate change, we are not helpless bystanders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It required grit and determination, and a belief that we needed to place environmental stewardship alongside socioeconomic growth and development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It required investment in infrastructure and capabilities that only the future generation can draw benefit from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It required making difficult trade-offs like setting aside financial resources, or transforming our industry, so that our limited resources work better for us in the long run.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Just like our water story, through long-term planning and careful deliberations, not only do we overcome our resource constraints, we turn our challenges into our strengths.

sections.label: Updating meritocracy
sections.summary: As meritocracy moved Singapore from Third World to First, it created winners passing on advantages, so work began over a decade ago to make meritocracy broader and more inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The escalator of meritocracy moved us from Third World to First.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But as we continued being successful and our framework of meritocracy created some winners who could pass on more opportunities and other advantages to their children, it became clear that we need our meritocracy to be updated and rebooted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need our meritocracy to be broader and more inclusive, if it were to remain fit for purpose for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, work on the next lap of meritocracy began more than a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And in Senior Minister Tharman's words back then, moving our society from a hierarchy of grades to a meritocracy of skills.

sections.label: Participatory meritocracy helping everyone keep up
sections.summary: It describes a broader, participatory meritocracy where every citizen helps others keep up so gaps never widen or become permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: One that is not only broader and more inclusive but also emanating from each citizen's basic responsibility, a meritocracy that is ever more participatory, a meritocracy in which every citizen is an active part of the solution, actively reaching back, helping each other keep up, so that even as the best among us run ahead, the gap is never pulled too wide and the gap is never permanent because everyone is helping everyone else to keep up.

sections.label: Focus on next generation
sections.summary: It says efforts must focus on children of those with less and break the transmission of disadvantages between generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And one final point I will make on this, is that in our efforts, we have to focus especially on the next generation, the children of those with less and make sure that they, the young ones in our framework of meritocracy, they especially can keep up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have got to double down on breaking the chain of transmission of disadvantages and stymied opportunities from one generation to the next.

sections.label: Sensitivity, understanding, careful words
sections.summary: It asks sensitivity to minorities, deeper mutual understanding, and care that words and deeds are not misused to cause division.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, for the majority race, I think it bears remembering always that it is harder to be a minority in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So let us be sensitive, reach out and strive for an ever deeper understanding of one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And third, for all of us, we should take extra effort to make sure that the words we utter and the deeds we do, would not end up being misconstrued, misappropriated or even weaponised by others to cause hurt and division especially in this world of social media.

sections.label: No ceiling for meritocracy
sections.summary: It states meritocracy has no ceiling and that those who reach the top have greater responsibility to help those at the bottom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In actual fact, our meritocracy encompasses a very important and fundamental social principle – that there is no ceiling for meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is our core consensus and commitment with regards to meritocracy, and it also implies that those who reach the top based on this consensus have a greater responsibility and obligation to help those at the bottom.

sections.label: Domestic views weakening multiculturalism
sections.summary: It says that even without foreign intervention, domestic views or behaviour may weaken Singapore's multiculturalism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even without foreign intervention, if we are not careful, domestic views or behaviour may become the very weapon that weakens our multiculturalism.

sections.label: Caution drawing conclusions from polls
sections.summary: It says polls show low confidence on some metrics but conclusions should be drawn circumspectly because survey question design can skew results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Actually, I have seen similar polls myself, polls that have not been cited in this debate, but polls that show confidence or optimism even in the single digits by percentage for certain metrics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But I think we got to be circumspect in drawing conclusions from these polls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For one, the design of survey questions itself is a notoriously difficult issue that can skew survey results.

sections.label: Core values meritocracy multiculturalism
sections.summary: The passage states that core values like meritocracy and multiculturalism were what the founding generation got right and allowed them to succeed and hand over Singapore today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have imbibed these values so much that sometimes, they just operate in the background and we do not realise that they are with us, that they are us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But these core values, like meritocracy and multiculturalism, were what our founding generation got right from the beginning and these allowed them – the founding generations, who had much fewer reasons, and much less resources to be confident about their future back then – these core values allowed them to pull through nonetheless, to succeed spectacularly and hand over to us the Singapore that we have today.

sections.label: Youths refresh Harmony Circles
sections.summary: Youths worked with Ms Nadin Samdin and the MCCY team to refresh IRCCs into new Harmony Circles, making them more diverse, youthful and digital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Youths like Nazhath Faheema, Benjamin Tan, Mohd Anas, Farisha Ishak and Joakim Gomez worked closely with Ms Nadin Samdin and I and my Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) team to refresh our Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) into our new Harmony Circles, making them more diverse, more youthful and more digital.

sections.label: Youth mental well-being initiatives
sections.summary: Ground-up youth initiatives drive the Singapore Mental Well-Being Network, with six Circles, 400 trained volunteers and around 30 partners, scaling up across community and workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Shane and Shamantha Yan's Growth Collective, Sabrina Ooi's Calm Collective, Simon Leow and Sherman Ho's Happiness Initiative, Asher Low's Limitless and Cho Ming Xiu's Campus PSY are just some of the many ground-up youth initiatives that are driving our Singapore Mental Well-Being Network in its efforts to raise awareness of and destigmatise mental well-being issues, as well as train peer supporters to support one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Nationally, we have thus far six of these Circles and counting, 400 trained volunteers and around 30 partners, and we are scaling up these efforts across the community and to workplaces.

sections.label: Youths participate in SG Green Plan
sections.summary: The passage states that youths are serious about tackling climate change and actively participate in the SG Green Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Our youths are also serious about tackling climate change and are actively participating in our SG Green Plan.

sections.label: Mentoring SG opportunities and partners
sections.summary: Mentoring SG has created 4,000 mentoring opportunities, supported 40 mentoring organisations and welcomed 13 corporate partners, with a new office to track outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mentoring SG has thus far created 4,000 mentoring opportunities for our youths, supported 40 mentoring organisations and welcomed 13 corporate partners and these numbers are growing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: When we set up the Mentoring SG office later this year, we will look to track the jobs and careers outcomes of our national mentoring efforts.

sections.label: Singapore robot intensive manufacturing
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore has the second-most robot intensive manufacturing sector in the world, just after South Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Singapore has the second-most robot intensive manufacturing sector in the world, just after South Korea.

sections.label: Agri-tech internships and automation support
sections.summary: Janice interned then got a full-time role in a Science Park agri-tech company supported by Enterprise Singapore schemes automating the agri-food tech sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: She explained to me how she first interned and then got a full-time role in one of the agri-tech companies located in our Science Park.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We are supporting these companies and workers like Janice through our Enterprise Singapore schemes as they deploy robotic arms and digital monitoring systems to automate our agri-food tech sector.

sections.label: Global Innovation Alliance and financial sector
sections.summary: Startups and SMEs can tap platforms like the Global Innovation Alliance, and the financial sector accounts for 14% of GDP and close to 200,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Startups and SMEs looking to grow beyond Singapore can also tap on platforms such as our Global Innovation Alliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Our financial sector is a bright spot in our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: It accounts for 14% of gross domestic product (GDP) and close to 200,000 jobs, with many offering higher wages relative to other sectors and we are continuing to grow the sector.

sections.label: Fixed Asset Investments over three years
sections.summary: Despite the pandemic, over S$51 billion in Fixed Asset Investments was attracted over the past three years, creating new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Despite the pandemic, we attracted over S$51 billion in Fixed Asset Investments (FAI) over the past three years and created new and exciting jobs in the sectors I have described earlier.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for lifelong skills
sections.summary: Use SkillsFuture to pick up skills throughout your lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Use SkillsFuture to pick up skills throughout your lifetime.

sections.label: Enabling environment for youths
sections.summary: The Ministry's addendum to the President's Address outlined plans to build an enabling environment for youths and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Like Gandalf, we must continue to provide a conducive and enabling environment for our Frodos – our youths, to learn, grow and thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Ministry's addendum to the President's Address outlined our Government's plans to continue to build such an environment for our youths and Singaporeans at large.

sections.label: Encouraging overseas Singaporeans to return
sections.summary: He encouraged overseas Singaporeans to stay overseas, explore and learn, but ultimately come home with skills, networks, ideas and organisations to build the country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: One of them asked me what opportunities are there for them back home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I encouraged them to stay overseas, explore, learn more, make their mark but always have Singapore in their minds and in their hearts; and to ultimately come home with the skills, networks, ideas and organisations they are building to build our country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: One of them which simply said, "we will".

sections.label: Large enterprises and PwD employment
sections.summary: Non-SMEs with turnover over S$100 million contribute 29% of enterprise employment, or 1.3 million jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Non-SMEs or enterprises with turnover exceeding S$100 million contribute to 29% of enterprise employment, or 1.3 million jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given their scale, even if only 1% of their workforce is committed to PwDs, 13,000 jobs will be created.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This equates to employment for 60% of the 21,000 PwDs of working age, who are still outside of the workforce.

sections.label: Disability inclusion company performance
sections.summary: The 45 companies that excelled in disability inclusion achieved higher revenue, double net income and higher profit margins.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The paper revealed that the 45 companies that excelled in disability inclusion achieved on average: (a) 28% higher revenue; (b) double the net income; and (c) 30% higher profit margins than the remaining companies.

sections.label: Typing assistance for disabled employee
sections.summary: An employer arranged typing assistance for a young man in a marketing role, who later got a government agency job at double pay.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The employer then made arrangements to provide this young man with assistance in typing tasks linked to the marketing role, allowing this staff to focus and eventually excel in client engagement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: He flourished in this lane and was eventually offered a job at a Government agency with double his original pay.

sections.label: Tender clause hiring vulnerable groups
sections.summary: A government tender clause required a percentage of project staff from vulnerable groups, and the PwDs hired stayed with the firm.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: There, he witnessed the real-world benefits of an inclusive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This MNC also became increasingly open to hire PwDs because of a government tender won.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This tender had a clause that stipulated for a percentage of project staff to be from vulnerable groups, such as seniors or disabled.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The good news is when the contract ended, all PwDs hired for the project continue to remain with the firm, and today seven years on, are still meaningfully employed.

sections.label: WP position on GST hike
sections.summary: The speaker says the WP opposed a GST hike from 7% to 9% in 2018 and never called for GST to be lowered to 0%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What I had said, and I will repeat that here, is that if you go back to those debates in Parliament in 2018, we opposed a hike of GST from 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At no point in that debate did we call for the GST to be lowered from 7% to 0%.

sections.label: GST hike debate and WP position
sections.summary: The speaker says that since the GST hike from 7% to 9% was first mooted in 2018, no one in the WP called for GST to be lowered to 0%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By the same token, I could bring up positions that the People's Action Party (PAP) has taken in the 1990s and table that for discussion here, such as the Graduate Mothers Scheme, such as votes for upgrading, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I think the point here is that – since the idea of a GST hike from 7% to 9% was first mooted and put on the table here in Parliament, which was in 2018 as I recall, at no point did anyone in the WP call for the GST to be lowered from 7% to 0%.

sections.label: GST increase decision timing
sections.summary: GST was raised from 5% to 7% around 2007, and the Government proposed raising it from 7% to 9% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And, in around 2007, it was increased from 5% to 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, I take it that as far as my learned friend, or rather, the hon Member Mr Perera is concerned, this implicit decision to accept GST was made in 2018 when the Government conveyed its decision to propose an increase of GST from 7% to 9%.

sections.label: COE prices and private hire cars
sections.summary: New COE records were set in larger car and open categories, and the Government said there is no evidence private hire car companies caused COE price increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: New records were also set in the larger car and open categories at $120,889 and $124,501 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: And I read that the latter is the highest price ever posted for any category of COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He said that these companies which grow their fleets aggressively and pushed up COE premiums in the process, are able to pass on the higher cost in the form of relatively small increases in daily rental rates while private buyers have to stomach the premium hike in one go, with a bigger loan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This is not a new issue and I am aware that the Government stated in a Parliamentary Question reply to my colleague, the hon Louis Chua, last year that there is no evidence that private hire car (PHC) companies have caused the increase in COE prices.

sections.label: Logistics companies cleaner vehicle transition
sections.summary: Amy Khor said work with logistics companies on cleaner vehicles is limited by availability of such vehicle technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor replied that, and I quote: "On logistics companies' transition to cleaner vehicles, we are working with them, but it is now limited by the availability of this kind of vehicles in terms of technology".

sections.label: Harbour craft decarbonisation targets
sections.summary: Under MPA's maritime decarbonisation blueprint, harbour craft will use low carbon energy by 2030 and full electric or net-zero fuels by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We should not let their emissions delay our zero-emission goals indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It is also commendable that MPA is working with Shell to allow other electric harbour craft to access their electric charges in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This is a first big step in the decarbonisation of the harbour craft fleet in the Port of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under MPA's maritime decarbonisation blueprint working towards 2050, all harbour craft will operate on low carbon energy solutions such as blended biofuels, for example, the B100 fuel, or hybrid diesel electric propulsion by 2030 and by 2050 will operate on full electric propulsion of net-zero fuels in order to achieve 15% reduction of 2021 levels by 2030, and 50% of 2021 levels by 2050.

sections.label: Shell Singapore capacity reduction
sections.summary: Shell announced in November 2021 it was halving crude processing capacity at its Singapore hub and reducing fuel exports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In my Budget debate's speech on 2022, I mentioned that Shell had, in November 2021, announced that it was halving its crude processing capacity at its Singapore hub and reducing fuel exports.

sections.label: Foreign worker and immigration flows
sections.summary: DPM Lawrence committed to manage foreign worker and immigration flows for Singaporeans' benefit and help newcomers integrate, while WP called for ITM report cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In his addendum, the Minister in-charge of the Strategy Group under the Prime Minister's Office, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence has committed to carefully manage foreign worker and immigration flows to ensure that these translate into tangible benefits for Singaporeans and separately, to help newcomers integrate better into society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP has also made calls for a report card on the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) and job outcomes for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Family offices and foreign wealth
sections.summary: The Government should closely look at the growth of family offices, inflows of foreign wealth and how Singaporeans are taking to these developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, another potential tinder box that the Government should look at closely is the growth of family offices, inflows of foreign wealth and how Singaporeans are taking to these developments.

sections.label: Openness and English test support
sections.summary: The speaker foresees greater openness to releasing information as fundamental to the refreshed social compact, and cites a CNA survey finding almost 80% favoured an English test for new PRs and citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, I foresee that a greater openness to releasing information will be fundamental to the refreshed social compact that the 4G Leadership seeks to forge with Singaporeans through the Forward Singapore (ForwardSG) exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A few weeks later, in a demographically representative poll of 500 Singapore-born citizens aged between 18 and 69, a CNA MediaCorp survey reported on 3 April this year by CNA found that almost 80% were in favour of an English test for new PRs and citizens.

sections.label: English requirement for foreign spouses
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that, all other things being equal, additional points or consideration be given for PR and citizenship to foreign spouses with working proficiency in English.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One legitimate concern, however, is the possible difficulty of an English requirement for foreign spouses who apply for PR or citizenship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My proposal calls for, all other things being equal, that additional points or consideration be given for PR and citizenship to foreign spouses who have a working proficiency in English.

sections.label: WP manifesto ideas considered
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government is actively considering some variation of WP manifesto ideas on anti-discrimination legislation, minimum wage and redundancy insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address Deputy Prime Minister Wong, if all we were doing was putting forward populist, unrealistic policies, we would not see the Government actively considering some variation of the WP manifesto ideas on anti-discrimination legislation, minimum wage and redundancy insurance.

sections.label: Verifying EP applicant qualifications
sections.summary: MOM announced that companies in Singapore would need to verify the educational qualifications of EP applicants from 1 September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 1 March this year, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) announced that companies in Singapore would need to verify the educational qualifications of EP applicants from 1 September 2023.

sections.label: Unmarried mothers' maternity leave
sections.summary: The Government announced that from January 2017 unmarried mothers would have 16 weeks of paid maternity leave and fathers two weeks of paid paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 9 November 2016, the Government announced that from January 2017, unmarried mothers would have 16 weeks of paid maternity leave, equal to their married counterparts and fathers would have two weeks of paid paternity leave.

sections.label: BTO priority status loss
sections.summary: The Government announced that first-time BTO applicants who give up their chance to select a flat would lose their priority status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 2 March this year, the Government announced that first-time BTO applicants who give up their chance to select a flat would lose their priority status.

sections.label: Supermarket plastic bag charge
sections.summary: The Government announced a plastic charge at most Singapore supermarkets from 3 July 2023, with two-thirds charging at least five cents per carrier bag.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 2 March this year, the Government announced a plastic charge at most Singapore supermarkets from 3 July 2023, with two-thirds of all supermarkets imposing a charge of at least five cents for each carrier bag.

sections.label: Tripartite guidelines on FWAs
sections.summary: MOM and the Tripartite Partners will introduce tripartite guidelines by 2024 requiring employers to consider FWA requests fairly and properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the course of this debate no less, Minister of State Gan Siow Huang has reiterated that to entrench FWAs, MOM and the Tripartite Partners will introduce a set of tripartite guidelines by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The guidelines would require employers to consider requests for FWAs fairly and properly.

sections.label: GST hike and corporate tax
sections.summary: The passage discusses alternatives to the GST hike from 7% to 9% and a domestic top-up tax raising multinationals' effective tax rate to 15% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a distraction and the PAP should be upfront about it since we have been clearly talking about the GST hike from 7% to 9%, and what alternatives there are for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is especially since the Government has announced at this year's Budget that it would implement a domestic top-up tax that will raise multinational enterprise groups' effective tax rate in Singapore to 15% in 2025 – less than two years from now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should the corporate tax revenues look respectable and sustainable for the short to medium term without any real compromise in our attractiveness to foreign investors, it may not be necessary to introduce another hike to the GST from 8% to 9% for 2024 if corporate tax revenue, which contribute 25% of our tax revenues today, goes up further.

sections.label: One-third non-PAP seats
sections.summary: The medium-term objective is to ensure that one-third of the seats in this House are not in the PAP's hands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our medium-term objective is to ensure that one-third of the seats in this House are not in the PAP's hands.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment two-thirds requirement
sections.summary: The Constitution can only be changed if two-thirds of the MPs in this House agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Constitution – the highest law of our land – which all other laws must take reference from, can only be changed if two-thirds of the MPs in this House agree.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment two-third majority votes
sections.summary: The PAP needs 63 votes in the House to pass a constitutional amendment with a two-third majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to pass a constitutional amendment with a two-third majority, the PAP needs 63 votes in this House.

sections.label: MPs present at constitutional amendment
sections.summary: Only 67 MPs were present when the constitutional amendment was passed on 21 March last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unbeknownst to many members of the public and voters, there were only 67 MPs in the House present when that constitutional amendment was passed on 21 March last month.

sections.label: PAP funding highlighted proposals
sections.summary: The PAP took the highlighted proposals on board and devoted fiscal and policy resources to fund and implement them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If these proposals that I have highlighted earlier were not serious, why did the PAP take them on board and devote fiscal resources to fund them and policy resources to implement them?

sections.label: Strong Opposition presence in House
