sections.summary: The inherent nature of power makes it wise to have at least one-third of the House in non-PAP Parties, given the possibility of a rogue PAP government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The inherent nature of power makes this unrealistic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, it is wise to have at least one-third of this House in a Party or Parties other than the PAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in the same vein as the Prime Minister alluded to in his speech in this debate, Singapore's future is not a given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It follows that no one can ignore the possibility of a rogue government springing from the bosom of the PAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our people should have real political options if or when that happens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are the reasons why there should be a strong Opposition presence in this House even before we talk of a change of government, alternative agendas and alternative budgets.

sections.label: Number of ICTs in 2020
sections.summary: On 6 July 2021, the Ministerial Statement provided that 4,200 ICTs worked in Singapore in 2020, a consistently small number.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I want to highlight the point that on his question on the number of ICTs, on 6 July 2021, in the Ministerial Statement, I had already provided the numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: There were 4,200 ICTs working in Singapore the year before – that is, 2020 – a number that has remained consistently small.

sections.label: Minister for Manpower on ICT numbers
sections.summary: In 2016, the Minister for Manpower answered that ICT numbers are not revealed, and low numbers could have punctured xenophobia early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera had – if my memory serves me correctly and I stand corrected, Mr Speaker, I am going based on memory alone – asked the question on the number of ICTs in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And the answer in Parliament from the Minister for Manpower was, "we don't reveal these numbers." And the point we were making – and the point I made in my speech again today – was if those numbers were released, because the numbers were low – they could have punctured all that xenophobia quite early.

sections.label: Releasing information early on racism
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government is better off providing more information rather than less on significant issues like racism or xenophobia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Some information, it is better for it to come out early and then we can move on, especially as you said when it concerns issues like racism or xenophobia, it is much better to credit early." Sir, I hope that response addresses the point put to me by the Minister for Manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I am suggesting that in certain issues of great significance, the Government is better off providing more information rather than less.

sections.label: Data graded confidential not released
sections.summary: The speaker says the data was graded confidential or secret and not ready for release, as releasing ICTs of a country may have ramifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If we had released, perhaps, it would have quelled all the xenophobia and all the raw emotions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But as Minister Tan See Leng said, that data was graded confidential or maybe even secret, I am not sure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But it was not ready for release, because when you release ICTs of a particular country, others may compare, it can have other ramifications.

sections.label: Ministers decided to release it
sections.summary: The Ministers had a serious discussion and said to release it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the end, these Ministers had a serious discussion and said "Let us release it".

sections.label: Other factors caused raw emotions
sections.summary: The speaker says many other factors took place resulting in the raw emotions, not the release.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If we are honest with ourselves, it is not because of that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It could have quelled it, but I think many other factors took place resulting in those raw emotions, which is most unfortunate.

sections.label: Populism and damage to Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says populism pretends there are simple answers to complex issues and would cause great damage to Singapore in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Populism is politics that pretends there are simple answers to complex issues, because there are not.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And if such populism were ever to take root in Singapore, well, in the short term, parties that push out such populist policies may gain some advantage, but in the longer term it will cause great damage to Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Opposition calling out Government
sections.summary: The speaker says if the Government falls short of these standards, the Opposition is expected to call it out.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If the Government were ever to fall short of these standards, we expect the Opposition to call us out and say so.

sections.label: Democracy, populism, political opportunism
sections.summary: The House stands for a maturing democracy with a serious Government and Opposition, rejecting populism and political opportunism in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If there is one thing that I hope all of us can take away from this debate and, given that there is, in fact, I would say, some common understanding of this, from what I hear from Mr Singh's speech, one outcome that we might be able to say to Singaporeans, it is this: that together in this House, both sides of the House, we stand for a democracy that is maturing, a serious Government and a serious Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We say yes to all that, but we say no to populism and political opportunism ever taking root in this House and in Singapore.

sections.label: Populism and opportunism both ways
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister's point on populism and opportunism should work both ways, not only against the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But insofar as populism and opportunism are concerned, I am quite certain that the Deputy Prime Minister means that it ought to work both ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It cannot be a case of pointing fingers at the Opposition and accusing them of that when certain actions of ruling party politicians on the ground are no better.

sections.label: Full employment and foreign talent
sections.summary: Singapore is at full employment with long-term unemployment at 0.6% to 0.7%, and foreign talent has increased jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, in Singapore, we are at full employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our long-term unemployment rate is at 0.6% to 0.7%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In fact, in my reports, as I have shared, for the year ending 2022, the number of resident employment, that means, locals – SCs, PRs – resident employment has gone up to even before pre-COVID-19 days, before 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In all of my interventions, in all of my speeches, I have consistently shared that for the foreign talent that have come in, it has resulted in an increase in the number of jobs created and employment opportunities for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Managing Director of consulting firm
sections.summary: The speaker declares being Managing Director and Partner of a management consulting firm working in digital, AI and skills development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, never mind, I will rest the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I declare that I am the Managing Director and Partner of a management consulting firm that does work in the areas of digital, artificial intelligence (AI) and skills development.

sections.label: Integrating training with transformed jobs
sections.summary: Decoupling training time from working time is less optimal than integrating training with jobs while jobs and companies are transformed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Decoupling training time and working time is less optimal than designing training to be integrated with their jobs while those jobs and the companies they belong to are being transformed.

sections.label: GenAI and ChatGPT growth
sections.summary: GenAI gained attention with technologies like DALL.E and Stable Diffusion, then grew massively with ChatGPT's November 2022 launch, reaching 1.6 billion visits in March.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: GenAI has been developing quietly for some time, gaining attention in recent years with the launch of technologies, like DALL.E, Image Generation, Mind Journey, Stable Diffusion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But it got a massive shot in the arm with the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, which became the fastest growing app in history, reaching 1.6 billion visits in March.

sections.label: GenAI drug discovery
sections.summary: Insilico Medicine used GenAI to identify a novel idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis drug candidate in 21 days, versus years traditionally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Insilico Medicine uses GenAI to identify a novel drug candidate for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in just 21 days, compared to years in traditional drug discovery.

sections.label: Singapore National AI Strategy
sections.summary: Singapore launched its National AI Strategy in 2019 with five National AI Projects and five ecosystem enablers, and AI Singapore will double AI Apprentices from 200 to 400.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore launched our National AI Strategy in 2019, which reflects our commitment to being a leader in developing and deploying scalable, impactful AI solutions, in key sectors of high value and relevance to our citizens and businesses along with five National AI Projects and five ecosystem enablers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: AI Singapore has partnered with businesses to nurture the development and adoption of AI models in key sectors like healthcare, transportation and finance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this year's COS, Minister Josephine Teo, shared that AI Singapore will double the number of AI Apprentices trained over the next five years from 200 to 400.

sections.label: Retrenchment support debate
sections.summary: During the Budget debate, the speaker raised considering retrenchment support, and Deputy Prime Minister Wong said targeted re-employment support is being considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: During this year's Budget debate, I raised that the time may have come to consider retrenchment support and Deputy Prime Minister Wong suggested in his speech that targeted re-employment support is being considered.

sections.label: Training workforce at scale
sections.summary: The speaker says far more than 400 people are involved and training programmes at scale and speed are needed for an AI-competitive workforce in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And sorry, but we are not talking 400 people here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, we will need training programmes at scale, at speed, to build a workforce that will be AI-competitive 10 years from now.

sections.label: Global AI rules and penalties
sections.summary: Over 60 countries and territories are considering some 800 measures; the Act sets rules, bans practices, and imposes penalties up to 6% of global revenues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: More than 60 plus countries and territories are considering some 800 measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Act sets out different rules and bans certain practices and imposes stiff penalties, up to 6% of a company's global revenues, for those in breach and the scope is global.

sections.label: AI governance and ethics actions
sections.summary: Four actions: invest in AI governance and ethics research, keep ethical guiderails and legal protections current, support responsible AI programmes, and serve as a global reference point.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One, invest in AI governance and ethics research; two, ensure that ethical guiderails and legal protections keep up with the rapid advancements in GenAI; three, support businesses in setting up responsible AI programmes; and four, serve as a global reference point to contribute to the development of global standards.

sections.label: AI disruption and togetherness
sections.summary: The passage calls for agreement on the common good, avoiding politicisation, and keeping AI strategies and people in pace with development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And hopefully, this time, we can all agree that it is for the common good and avoid its politicisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I agree with Dr Tan Wu Meng, that in a world of AI disruption, togetherness and trust is more important than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need our AI strategies, policies and people to keep pace with the breathless development; so, let us buckle up!

sections.label: Core values of Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states that she reaffirmed core values of fairness, inclusivity, mutual support, equality and belonging for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In doing so, she reaffirmed the core values of Singaporeans: fairness, inclusivity, mutual support, equality and a sense of belonging for all regardless of background so that every Singaporean is afforded the opportunity to achieve his or her full potential.

sections.label: Equal progress for all Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states that progress belongs to all Singaporeans regardless of race, language or religion, with equal schools, hospitals and housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: First, this belongs to all Singaporeans, regardless of race, language, religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Second, when there is progress, we ensure that the progress is spread equally, regardless of race, language or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: There will be the same schools for all, the same hospitals for all, the same low-cost housing for all – regardless of whether you are brown, black, yellow, green or any other spectrum of the rainbow.

sections.label: Faisal Manap and grassroots advisor role
sections.summary: The passage states Mr Faisal Manap will not explain difficult Government policies or convince residents of long-term interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Faisal Manap had also made comments about wanting to have the resources of a PA network and to be able to do things like give out Edusave awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: He is not going to do the equally important work of explaining difficult Government policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: He is not going to go out into the community and explain the need for GST to be increased or for public transport fares to be adjusted or for any number of popular but vital and important policies, where as community leaders, we have to convince residents that the long-term interests of Singapore are best served by taking these steps.

sections.label: Faisal Manap and grassroots advisor honesty
sections.summary: The passage states Mr Faisal Manap cannot be grassroots advisor when disagreeing with Government policies, and notes DPM Lawrence's five key shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If Mr Faisal Manap is going to be honest about this issue, he needs to admit that he cannot fulfil the role of grassroots advisor on behalf of the Government when he disagrees with so many of the Government's policies and with how the Government raises money to fund its progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It also handles the difficult work of engaging the public on the hard truths involved in making our society harmonious, peaceful and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence laid out five key shifts to create a stronger social compact to take Singapore forward.

sections.label: Growing vibrant innovative economy
sections.summary: The passage states that first, a vibrant and innovative economy must be grown.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, we must grow a vibrant and innovative economy.

sections.label: COVID-19 Budgets and past Reserves
sections.summary: During COVID-19, five Budgets were rolled out in one year and about $40 billion was drawn from past Reserves without borrowing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: During the COVID-19 crisis, we rolled out five Budgets in one year and eventually drew down around $40 billion from past Reserves to save lives and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Most remarkably, we did not borrow a single cent, which would have burdened future generations.

sections.label: Building resources for future generations
sections.summary: The passage says capability and resources must be built up for future generations, and questions the WP's rejection of the GST hike.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must do our best to build up the capability and resources for future generations of Singaporeans, just as the previous generations had done for us.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why we should think carefully when the WP says that they reject the GST hike because one alternative that they have been constantly offering is to increase the proportion used from returns on investments.

sections.label: Technology supply chains fragmenting
sections.summary: As countries realise technology's critical importance, technological supply chains will increasingly bifurcate and fragment into competing blocs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, as countries realise the critical importance of technology, technological supply chains will increasingly bifurcate and fragment into competing blocs.

sections.label: Singapore raising taxes for social needs
sections.summary: Singapore faces similar challenges and will have to make difficult policy moves like raising taxes to support growing social needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singapore is facing similar challenges, and we will have to make difficult policy moves like raising taxes to support growing social needs.

sections.label: ITM 2.0 additional pillars
sections.summary: ITM 2.0 includes two additional pillars, resilience and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: ITM 2.0 includes two additional pillars – resilience and sustainability.

sections.label: Singapore innovative economies ranking
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked among the top 10 most innovative economies in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singapore is ranked among the top 10 most innovative economies in the world.

sections.label: World Bank ranks Singapore
sections.summary: The World Bank ranks Singapore as the best place in the world for a child to realise his or her potential.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The World Bank ranks Singapore as the best place in the world for a child to realise his or her potential.

sections.label: Learning Society and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Singapore will strengthen the SkillsFuture movement to ensure Singaporeans are resilient and well-equipped for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must, as Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence said, strive to be a "Learning Society – from cradle to grave".

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will strengthen our SkillsFuture movement to ensure Singaporeans are resilient and well-equipped to face the future.

sections.label: Openness captures new value
sections.summary: Remaining open in this era of contestation enables Singapore to capture new value and flows and strengthen capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Remaining open in this era of contestation enables Singapore to capture new value and flows and strengthen our capabilities.

sections.label: Global Innovation Alliance network
sections.summary: The Global Innovation Alliance, a network of 17 innovation hotspots, has enabled entrepreneurs to incubate ideas and find partners overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our Global Innovation Alliance – a network of 17 innovation hotspots around the world – has enabled our entrepreneurs to incubate their ideas and find partners overseas.

sections.label: Government addresses inequality and competition
sections.summary: The Government is addressing wealth inequality, job competition and unfair workplace practices by adjusting policies and frameworks while refining openness.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We may also be concerned about wealth inequality, more severe competition for jobs, or even unfair workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These are issues that the Government is addressing, by adjusting our policies, strengthening our frameworks and developing Singaporeans fully.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our commitment to openness remains unchanged, but we, too, can refine our approach to openness to ensure that it is fit for the times.

sections.label: Requirements on foreign talent
sections.summary: Specific requirements have been stipulated to address the quality of foreign talents and prevent concentration in certain sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I understand that Singaporeans are worried and concerned about these issues.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have stipulated specific requirements to address the quality of foreign talents and to prevent concentration in certain sectors.

sections.label: Securing Singapore's future unity
sections.summary: Securing Singapore's future requires transforming the economy, harnessing technology, caring for the vulnerable and middle, and staying united.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the coming years, securing our future will require us to continue transforming our economy and creating new opportunities for our people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must continue to have this spirit of pushing our frontiers, to harness technology and innovation to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must take care of the most vulnerable segments of our society, while ensuring that our broad middle continue to see improvements in their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we must continue to build on the foundation of our national pledge – "regardless of race, language or religion" – to stay united in this contested world while deepening connections with people around the world.

sections.label: Pew survey on Singapore unity
sections.summary: A 2022 Pew Research Centre survey found Singapore less divided and more united after coming out of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In a 2022 survey by the Pew Research Centre on how advanced economies were affected by COVID-19, Singapore was found to be less divided and more united, after coming out of COVID-19.

sections.label: Constitution and minority rights council
sections.summary: The Constitution requires the government to regard racial and religious minority interests, and the PCMR scrutinises legislation for disadvantage to any community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our founding leaders, for instance, set out in our Constitution, the most basic document that we have in Singapore, for the government of the day to always have regard for the interests of our racial and religious minorities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We set up the Presidential Council on Minority Rights (PCMR).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In almost no other place in the world is there an institution like the PCMR, whose role is to scrutinise legislation after they are passed in this House to ensure that they are not disadvantageous to any particular racial or religious community.

sections.label: Ethnic Integration Policy in housing
sections.summary: The Ethnic Integration Policy gives a balanced ethnic mix in public housing, so Singapore does not have racial enclaves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our Ethnic Integration Policy allows us to have a balanced ethnic mix in our public housing, so that we do not have racial enclaves like we see in many other countries.

sections.label: Edelman Trust Barometer decline
sections.summary: The most recent Edelman Trust Barometer shows trust decreasing in many countries, in government, businesses, media and non-governmental organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The most recent edition of the Edelman Trust Barometer shows that trust continues to decrease in many countries around the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Not just trust in government, but in all institutions – businesses, the media and even in non-governmental organisations.

sections.label: Unite pillar of exercise
sections.summary: The Unite pillar brings Singaporeans together to explore what keeps them going as one people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One pillar of this exercise is the "Unite" pillar, where we bring Singaporeans together to explore what keeps us going as one people.

sections.label: Unity embedded in daily life
sections.summary: Unity is achieved not by ideas alone but by embedding it in daily life, work and socialising.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One key takeaway is that this unity is not an abstract concept – unity, cohesion, harmony – sometimes, if you do not pay attention, you might think it is just an abstract concept, but it is not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And we achieve it not by ideas alone, but more importantly, by having it embedded in our daily lives: part and parcel of what we do, where we go, who we see and the people we socialise and work with.

sections.label: Breaking down social barriers
sections.summary: Stronger unity needs occasions and opportunities for people of different backgrounds to spend time together and break down barriers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The key to fostering stronger unity is to have both occasion and opportunity for people from different backgrounds to see and enjoy spending time with one another, through the passions that they pursue so that we are not stratified and constantly in our own social circles only and in our own echo chambers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Stratification is very unhealthy and it can lead to entrenched intergenerational stratification as well if we are not careful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, we need to break down these barriers, not just along racial or religious lines but also between other fault lines in our society – like local and foreigner, the different income groups, between the young and old, as well as intergenerational conflict.

sections.label: Religious institutions working together
sections.summary: Religious institutions work together to benefit neighbourhoods and let congregations intermix and know each other.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Many of our religious institutions work together, to benefit their neighbourhoods and in so doing, provide opportunities for their congregation to intermix and to get to know each other.

sections.label: Refreshed Harmony Circles
sections.summary: MCCY has recently refreshed its Racial and Religious Harmony Circles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To this end, MCCY has also recently refreshed our Racial and Religious Harmony Circles.

sections.label: Racial and Religious Harmony Month
sections.summary: From this year, July is dedicated as Racial and Religious Harmony Month to highlight Harmony Circles and community partners and organise activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Starting from this year, we will also be dedicating July as our Racial and Religious Harmony Month – not just a day but a month, to highlight the efforts of our Harmony Circles and our community partners and organise more activities to celebrate and to promote racial and religious harmony, so that the significance of the day and of the occasion and the learning points go beyond just spending a day celebrating one another's special occasions – coming in a different attire, perhaps, or costume, celebrating by exchanging goodies and gifts associated with festivities of other races.

sections.label: Strategic Partnership CCA initiative
sections.summary: The Strategic Partnership CCA initiative lets secondary students join CCAs outside their own schools, increasing CCA variety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But there is no reason why this same configuration should also hold for co-curricular activities (CCAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the Strategic Partnership CCA initiative allows secondary students to join in various CCAs outside of their own schools, increasing the variety of the CCAs that students will have access to.

sections.label: DSMP and PwD sport participation
sections.summary: The DSMP, launched in 2016, contributed to sport participation among PwDs rising from 28% in 2015 to 50% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Launched in 2016, the DSMP has contributed to increased sport participation rates among PwDs, rising from 28% in 2015 to 50% in 2019.

sections.label: Sport Excellence Scholarship support
sections.summary: The spexScholarship is offered to athletes with potential to excel at major games or world-level events, granting allowance, benefits, sport science and sport medicine access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A key part of this ecosystem and this plan is the Sport Excellence Scholarship (spexScholarship) which is offered to our athletes with the potential to excel at major games or world-level events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Many of you, I am sure, would have been very proud to have seen her break her records, making great strides recently, quite literally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: She spent some time away from the spexScholarship, but after a while, having discussed with her coach and the National Sports Association, decided to come back full-time and was supported by the spexScholarship, which grants her an allowance and benefits, and allows her to access support to sport science and sport medicine.

sections.label: ActiveSG credits for children
sections.summary: At Budget 2023, an additional $100 of credits was announced for ActiveSG accounts of children aged four to 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Recently, at Budget 2023, I had announced that we will put in an additional $100 of credits in the ActiveSG accounts of children aged four to 12, so that they can start accessing these programmes, not just for fitness but from a social mixing perspective from an early age.

sections.label: Working English as limiting factor
sections.summary: The speaker's view is that working-level English knowledge should not be a defining or limiting factor as a single-point test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think there is range for a variety of different views on what weight you might place on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But my own view is that the knowledge of English at a working level, while helpful, should not be a defining or, indeed, a limiting factor, which might happen if you introduce it as a single-point test.

sections.label: No single-point English test
sections.summary: Singapore currently has no single-point English test or proficiency requirement for naturalisation, unlike some other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I believe these are equally, if not perhaps in some cases, more effective as a marker of integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We currently do not have a single-point English test or proficiency requirement for naturalisation, unlike some other countries.

sections.label: Constitution naturalisation language marker
sections.summary: The Constitution provides that one marker for naturalisation is working knowledge of any of the four official languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, as Mr Pritam Singh would appreciate, the Constitution itself currently provides that one of the markers for naturalisation is working knowledge of any of the four official languages.

sections.label: Youth panels introduction
sections.summary: Youth panels will be introduced later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: With this in mind, we will introduce youth panels later this year.

sections.label: MCCY sponsoring White or Green Paper
sections.summary: MCCY can consider sponsoring a White or Green Paper on the proposal for debate in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MCCY can consider sponsoring a White or Green Paper on the proposal, so that they can be considered in this House and we can then all have a robust debate on them.

sections.label: Sembawang seniors mobility project
sections.summary: A project started in 2022 reaches less mobile seniors in Sembawang with activities to improve mobility and cognitive functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Started in 2022, this project reaches out to the less mobile seniors in Sembawang, with activities that helped to improve their mobility as well as their cognitive functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And it was borne of her realisation that perhaps the seniors were less connected and had less resources available to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This was done as part of a volunteering programme with the Agency for Integrated Care and Blossom Seeds Limited, a charity operating in that area.

sections.label: National Museum of Singapore exhibition
sections.summary: Members are encouraged to visit an exhibition at the National Museum of Singapore, free for Singaporeans and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I encourage Members here in this House to visit it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is at the National Museum of Singapore and it is free for Singaporeans and PRs.

sections.label: Singapore's lack of natural resources
sections.summary: Singapore lacks natural resources, a natural hinterland and space, and has done better with its people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do not have natural resources and we do not have the blessings of a natural hinterland that we can take advantage of or, indeed, space – which comes at a significant premium for us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have always done much better, punched above our weight, gone further with our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we will see a vibrant, thriving Singapore for generations to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I did not say that an English requirement would be a single point of consideration for PRs and new citizenship applications.

sections.label: Survey on English and economic contributions
sections.summary: A survey found the ability to communicate in English ranked number one, shared with economic contributions to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Minister referred to various criteria that we broadly know, with respect to immigration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But that survey found that the ability to communicate in English ranks number one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In fact, the number one position was shared with economic contributions to Singapore.

sections.label: Academic element in school entry
sections.summary: The speaker says there is an academic element to entry into Singapore schools and the two tests should not be conflated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Because there is an academic element to their entry into the schools in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, I do not think one should conflate the two different tests.

sections.label: Three short points in speech
sections.summary: The speaker says he will make only three short points and thanks Members who spoke on the Government's plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Hon Members will be happy to note that I will only make three short points in my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, I wish to thank the hon Members who spoke for sharing their valuable insights about the Government's plans outlined by the President.

sections.label: Unanimity on retaining core values
sections.summary: The speaker notes unanimity among Members on retaining core values ingrained by founding leaders and useful for generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the diversity of the topics covered in this debate, I noted unanimity amongst hon Members on the importance of retaining our core values that have been ingrained in our nation by our founding generation of leaders and stood us in good stead for several generations.

sections.label: Members' suggestions for future plans
sections.summary: The speaker says Members' suggestions deserve examination for incorporation into laid-out future plans, citing linking unemployment support to skills upgrading and job searching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Moving on to my second point, I wish to highlight that hon Members had provided a surfeit of suggestions in this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: These suggestions deserve examination with a view to see if the future plans of this Government that have already been laid out, can be further strengthened by their incorporation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: They include: Linking unemployment support for citizens with their agreement to undertake skills upgrading and active job searching – a suggestion raised jointly by the hon Member Mr Desmond Choo.

sections.label: Caregiving leave and inclusive hiring ideas
sections.summary: The speaker lists caregiving leave for elderly parents and inclusive hiring of PwDs as Members' ideas, and notes Members lamented suggestions not taken up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Providing caregiving leave to take care of elderly parents – an idea of the hon Member Ms Poh Li San; and Encouraging our non-SMEs to embrace inclusive hiring and employ more PwDs – an idea floated and passionately argued by the hon Member Miss Rachel Ong Several hon Members from across the aisle lamented that their suggestions have not been taken up by the Government.

sections.label: Executive balancing factors in implementation
sections.summary: The speaker says the Executive bears responsibility for governing and must balance policy intent, competing viewpoints and resourcing priorities when assessing Members' ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I think we can all appreciate that, in assessing the viability of implementing ideas from hon Members, the Executive arm of our Government bears the heavy responsibility of governing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: They have to strike a balance between a wide range of factors including policy intent, competing viewpoints and resourcing priorities.

sections.label: Government agnostic on ideas
sections.summary: The Government has stated many times that it is agnostic about who and where good ideas come from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The Government has unequivocally stated on many occasions that it is agnostic as to who and where good ideas come from.
